# Reproducibility

## Environment

- Python 3.10 or newer
- No GPU
- No external service for default runs
- No API key for default runs

Install the development environment.

```bash
python -m pip install -e ".[dev]"
```

## Required checks

```bash
pytest
python -m worldmodel_lstar.run --config configs/dfa_small.yaml
python -m worldmodel_lstar.run --config configs/rest_auth_small.yaml
python -m worldmodel_lstar.evaluate --config configs/eval_small.yaml
```

## Determinism

Configurations include explicit seeds. Environments are deterministic and reset before each experiment. Candidate generation order is stable. Tie-breaking uses experiment cost and identifier.

## Evidence

Keep the complete run directory for every reported result. Do not report aggregate tables without retaining the matching configs, JSONL traces, learned models, and software revision.

## Publication checklist

1. Record the repository commit
2. Freeze dependency versions
3. Run at least three independent seeds per target family
4. Report target generation and exclusions
5. Include uncertainty intervals
6. Audit failed runs
7. Verify that unsafe actions were simulated only
8. Complete a related-work and license review
9. Archive raw artifacts
10. Separate preregistered hypotheses from exploratory analysis

documents.title: lineagerag — README.md
documents.content:
# LineageRAG

Copy-aware evidence corroboration for retrieval-augmented verification

[![Python 3.11+](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.11%2B-2563eb)](https://www.python.org/)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-16a34a)](LICENSE)
[![Offline first](https://img.shields.io/badge/runtime-offline-0f766e)](#quick-start)

LineageRAG asks a simple question before treating agreement as confidence:

> Did these documents reach the same conclusion independently, or did they copy one another?

Twenty pages can repeat one mistaken bulletin. A verifier that counts URLs sees twenty
witnesses. LineageRAG infers likely derivation links, collapses dependent documents into
origin families, and combines evidence at the family level.

The repository is a complete CPU-only research system. It generates controlled evidence
cascades, trains a calibrated dependency classifier, infers sparse document genealogy,
trains dataset-specific stance models, runs copy-aware Bayesian verification, compares
baselines, and produces an interactive evidence graph. Smoke mode needs no API key, GPU,
model download, or external dataset.

## Why source count is not evidence count

Domain and URL deduplication address repeated locations. Near-duplicate filtering catches
almost identical text. Neither is enough when copied information crosses domains, receives
a heavy rewrite, preserves a rare factual error, or cites a common upstream report.

LineageRAG estimates dependence from observable signals:

- publication order
- citation and quotation links
- exact and paraphrased text overlap
- stable SimHash similarity
- entity and number overlap
- shared rare error markers
- URL, domain, and title similarity

The resulting weighted graph is clustered into likely origin families. A bounded family
weight prevents copied descendants from contributing linearly to the claim posterior.

```text
Retrieved documents
        |
        v
Observable pair features
        |
        v
Directed lineage graph
        |
        v
Evidence families
        |
        v
Family-level Bayesian verifier
        |
        +--> claim posterior
        +--> effective evidence count
        +--> false-corroboration risk
        +--> next independent search intent
```

## Quick start

Python 3.11 or newer is required.

```bash
python -m venv .venv
```

Activate the environment on Linux or macOS:

```bash
source .venv/bin/activate
```

Activate it on Windows PowerShell:

```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
```

Install and validate the project:

```bash
python -m pip install -e ".[dev]"
pytest -q
```

Run the complete benchmark:

```bash
python -m lineagerag.cli smoke --seed 14 --out artifacts/smoke
python -m lineagerag.cli inspect-run artifacts/smoke
```

The smoke run creates at least 200 claims and 2,000 documents across nine controlled
cascade templates. It evaluates LineageRAG and ten non-oracle baselines.

## Interactive genealogy

Open the generated file in any modern browser:

```text
artifacts/smoke/evidence_genealogy.html
```

The demo is standalone. Plotly is embedded into the file, so the graph works without a
network connection.

Node fill identifies a predicted origin family. The border shows stance. Diamond nodes
are inferred roots. The summary cards compare raw source count with effective evidence.

## CLI

```bash
# Generate a reusable synthetic corpus with hidden oracle annotations
python -m lineagerag.cli generate-synthetic \
  --config configs/synthetic.yaml \
  --out data/synthetic

# Run the configured benchmark
python -m lineagerag.cli evaluate \
  --config configs/synthetic.yaml \
  --out artifacts/synthetic

# Copy a completed standalone demo
python -m lineagerag.cli demo \
  --run artifacts/smoke \
  --out artifacts/demo

# Register a separately acquired local dataset
python -m lineagerag.cli prepare averitec \
  --source /path/to/local/data \
  --out data/averitec

# Train the calibrated dependency model
python -m lineagerag.cli train-lineage \
  --out models/dependency.json

# Run both held-out real claim benchmarks
python -m lineagerag.cli evaluate-real \
  --scifact-source data/external/scifact \
  --averitec-source data/external/averitec/AVeriTeC-7c62d1ec8df3fb560d6efe2b85fa191135636f81 \
  --lineage-model models/dependency.json \
  --out artifacts/real

# Build and test chronological OpenAlex citation cascades
python -m lineagerag.cli evaluate-citations \
  --scifact-source data/external/scifact \
  --lineage-model models/dependency.json \
  --out artifacts/citations
```

Real-data adapters never access the network or redistribute data. The explicit PowerShell
acquisition script downloads pinned sources only after license acceptance and checks each
archive hash. The offline benchmark remains available without research data.

## Method

For each document pair $i, j$, a transparent logistic model estimates a shared-derivation
probability from observed features:

```math
p_{ij} = \sigma(b + w^\top x_{ij})
```

The default trained model uses claim-disjoint synthetic graphs. A second seed provides
probability calibration and an operating threshold chosen for high validation precision.
An auditable hand-specified scorer remains available for offline smoke tests.

Edges above the calibrated threshold form a directed graph. Explicit citations determine
direction first, followed by publication order. Copy-family inference keeps at most one
parent per document to reduce bridge errors.

Within each predicted family $f$, document stances are pooled into a family score
$s_f \in [-1, 1]$. The support posterior is:

```math
\mathrm{logit}\,P(y=1 \mid E)
=
\mathrm{logit}\,P(y=1)
+
\sum_f 1.6\,w_f\,s_f
```

The effective family weight grows slowly with copied descendants:

```math
w_f
=
c_f
\min
\left(
1 + \alpha \log(1 + |f| - 1),
\tau
\right)
```

Here $c_f$ combines stance confidence, lineage confidence, and configurable source
reliability. The cap $\tau$ is the key safeguard. One family cannot gain unbounded
influence by producing more copies.

Dataset-specific stance classifiers use TF-IDF features and logistic regression. Training,
validation, and test claims are disjoint. Each method receives its own validation-fitted
claim-probability calibrator.

## Benchmark design

The generator provides nine graph families:

- independent witnesses
- copied bulletin star
- citation chain
- paraphrase tree
- cross-domain syndication
- shared false root
- delayed correction cascade
- two-origin merge
- mixed support and refute families

Observed document metadata and hidden oracle annotations are saved separately. Inference
receives documents and extracted stances only. Oracle files are read during metric
calculation and by explicit upper-bound baselines.

Synthetic text mutations include exact copying, attributed quotes, light and heavy
paraphrases, entity-preserving rewrites, number changes, title rewrites, summaries, and
boilerplate insertion.

## Baselines

All methods use the same claims, retrieval order, stance observations, and evaluator.

| Method | What it controls |
|---|---|
| Standard RAG | Counts every selected document independently |
| URL deduplication | Removes repeated URLs |
| Domain deduplication | Keeps one document per domain |
| Domain and near duplicate | Applies both simple controls together |
| Near-duplicate deduplication | Removes very high lexical similarity |
| MMR diversity | Trades relevance for lexical diversity |
| Reliability weighted | Weights sources by agreement and ignores lineage |
| Contradiction aware | Balances support and refuting stances |
| Reliability and contradiction | Combines the preceding controls |
| Counterfactual evidence | Preserves evidence from both sides |
| LineageRAG | Discounts likely derivation families |

Oracle family baselines are included only as diagnostic upper bounds.

## Research data

Raw external data is excluded from Git. Source URL, upstream commit, license, archive
checksum, and local destination are recorded under `data/manifests`.

| Resource | Role | Split | License |
|---|---|---|---|
| SciFact | Scientific claims and direct document stance | Official dev test | CC BY 4.0 and ODC-By 1.0 |
| AVeriTeC | Real web claims and annotated evidence URLs | Chronological 70/15/15 | CC BY-NC 4.0 |
| OpenAlex | Citation links and publication dates | Chronological 60/20/20 | CC0 |

Review the terms before downloading. AVeriTeC is noncommercial.

```powershell
.\scripts\acquire_research_data.ps1 -AcceptResearchLicenses
```

See [docs/real_data.md](docs/real_data.md) for normalization, leakage controls, and
limitations.

## Latest research result

The overall kill criterion fails. This is an important result, not a hidden caveat.

| Evaluation | Size | LineageRAG result | Comparator or interpretation |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Learned synthetic | 200 claims | Brier 0.165, false corroboration 0.000 | Controlled sanity check |
| SciFact | 300 test claims | Brier 0.162 | Combined dedup 0.164, paired interval excludes zero |
| AVeriTeC | 536 test claims | Brier 0.185 | Combined dedup 0.187, paired interval includes zero |
| OpenAlex | 8 test cascades | Citation edge F1 1.000 | Explicit citation is an input feature |

SciFact passes the held-out calibration criterion. AVeriTeC does not establish a
statistically reliable improvement. OpenAlex confirms citation metadata handling, not
hidden copying detection.

On learned synthetic cascades, iterative search uses 7.58 documents per claim on average
instead of all 11.15 available documents. It reaches both stopping thresholds for 67 of
200 claims. The remaining 133 claims stop at the explicit budget limit.

Classification quality is still weak. SciFact accuracy is 0.373 with 0.990 abstention.
AVeriTeC accuracy is 0.347 with 0.466 abstention. This version is a research prototype,
not a fact-checking product.

See [reports/research_summary.md](reports/research_summary.md) and
[reports/latest_results.json](reports/latest_results.json) for exact values.

## Outputs

Every completed run contains:

| Artifact | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `metrics.json` | Run metadata and all method metrics |
| `metrics_by_method.csv` | Method comparison |
| `metrics_by_template.csv` | Breakdown by cascade type |
| `lineage_metrics.json` | Edge and family recovery |
| `claim_results.csv` | Claim-level predictions |
| `predicted_edges.csv` | Inferred directed graph edges |
| `predicted_families.csv` | Predicted family membership |
| `trajectories.jsonl` | Active-search decisions |
| `calibration.png` | Reliability diagram |
| `false_corroboration_by_template.png` | Failure-rate comparison |
| `evidence_genealogy.html` | Standalone interactive graph |
| `summary.md` | Run report and kill-criterion check |

## Metrics

Claim verification uses accuracy, macro F1, Brier score, negative log likelihood,
expected calibration error, abstention rate, search cost, and false-corroboration rate.

Lineage recovery uses edge precision, recall, F1, area under the precision-recall curve,
adjusted Rand index, normalized mutual information, pairwise family F1, and
independent-family recall.

A false-corroboration event requires all of the following:

1. The method assigns high support probability
2. The claim is false, mixed, or unsupported
3. Several retrieved documents support the claim
4. Hidden lineage shows fewer than the required number of independent support origins

## Reproducibility

Randomness enters only through the synthetic generator and seeded bootstrap utilities.
The seed is stored in every run. Stable hashing is used for text features, so Python hash
randomization does not change lineage scores.

See [docs/reproducibility.md](docs/reproducibility.md) for exact commands, artifact
schemas, and extension points.

## Research boundaries

The bundled benchmark is a controlled engineering test. Synthetic markers make lineage
recoverable and overstate performance compared with natural publication cascades.

The supervised stance models are lightweight and do not provide the language understanding
needed for deployment. Source reliability estimates have limited coverage. Time metadata
can be missing, delayed, or manipulated.

AVeriTeC provides evidence URLs but no gold copying families. OpenAlex citations are
relationships, not copying labels. Natural news genealogy remains unverified.

The paired AVeriTeC confidence interval includes zero, so the strict project kill criterion
fails for this release. News lineage inference should be redesigned rather than promoted.

## Repository policy

This repository contains an original implementation, generated synthetic data, and
project-authored documentation. It does not include third-party papers, external datasets,
model weights, copied code, or reproduced result tables.

See [NOTICE](NOTICE) and [docs/originality.md](docs/originality.md) for the source boundary.

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome for learned lineage models, temporal cascade adapters, calibrated
stance models, and evaluation datasets with clear redistribution terms.

Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) before opening a pull request.

## License

LineageRAG is released under the [MIT License](LICENSE).

documents.content:
# Synthetic evidence cascade dataset card

## Purpose

The bundled generator tests whether a verifier distinguishes repeated documents from
independent evidence. It is designed for software validation, controlled ablations, and
failure analysis.

## Composition

The default smoke configuration generates 200 claims and more than 2,000 documents across
nine graph templates. Each claim has observed documents and stance observations. Oracle
edges, families, and stances are written to separate files.

## Generation

All people, organizations, projects, domains, and events are fictional. Text is assembled
from repository-authored templates and deterministic mutations.

## Intended use

- lineage inference unit tests
- copy-robust verification research
- calibration experiments
- active retrieval policy tests

## Out-of-scope use

The dataset must not be used to claim real-world fact-checking performance, source
credibility, political truthfulness, or misinformation prevalence.

## Known bias

Synthetic rare-error markers and regular publication times make some derivation links easier
than natural data. The language is narrow and does not represent multilingual, scientific,
social, or adversarial writing.

## External evaluation data

The real-data protocol for SciFact, AVeriTeC, and OpenAlex is documented in
[real_data.md](real_data.md). None of those raw sources are distributed with this
repository.

documents.content:
# LineageRAG model card

## Model details

LineageRAG 0.1 is a deterministic pipeline rather than a trained foundation model. It uses
hand-specified pair features, a logistic edge score, graph connected components, lexical
stance observations, and a bounded family-level Bayesian verifier.

## Inputs

- a claim
- retrieved documents
- publication metadata
- citations and quotations when available
- stance observations

## Outputs

- predicted claim label
- support probability
- raw support and refute counts
- effective family-level counts
- predicted lineage edges and families
- false-corroboration risk
- independent-search intent

## Performance

No fixed performance values are shipped as scientific claims. Run the benchmark to produce
versioned local metrics. Synthetic smoke results are engineering checks only.

## Limitations

The edge model is not calibrated for open-web data. The lexical stance extractor cannot
handle nuanced entailment. Connected-component clustering is sensitive to bridge errors.
Publication times can be missing or manipulated. Source reliability defaults are
illustrative.

## Ethical considerations

The system should support human review, not automate credibility judgments about people or
publishers. Family inference is probabilistic and can incorrectly associate independent
authors. Preserve source context and provide an appeal path in any applied system.

documents.title: lineagerag — docs/real_data.md
documents.content:
# Real data protocol

LineageRAG uses three external research resources. Their raw files and cached API
responses are excluded from Git. The repository stores only acquisition metadata,
normalization code, and derived aggregate results.

## SciFact

SciFact provides scientific claims, document abstracts, document-level stance labels,
and sentence rationales. The official development set is the untouched test set. The
final 20 percent of training claim IDs form the validation set.

The claim and annotation files use CC BY 4.0. Corpus abstracts use ODC-By 1.0.
See [the official SciFact repository](https://github.com/allenai/scifact).

SciFact does not provide a trustworthy claim publication date. Its experiment is
therefore an official split, not a temporal split.

## AVeriTeC

AVeriTeC provides real web claims, claim dates, verdicts, and annotated question and
answer evidence with source URLs. Claims from the official train and development files
are sorted by parsed claim date and divided chronologically into 70 percent training,
15 percent validation, and 15 percent test.

Document stance is weak supervision. Each annotated evidence document inherits the
claim-level verdict for model training and scoring. This is noisier than SciFact's direct
document stance labels and is reported as a limitation.

AVeriTeC uses CC BY-NC 4.0. The project is research-only with respect to this data.
See [the official AVeriTeC repository](https://github.com/MichSchli/AVeriTeC).

## OpenAlex

SciFact evidence-paper titles are matched to OpenAlex works. Each local cascade contains
the matched work, up to two referenced works, and up to four works that cite it. Root
publication date defines a chronological 60/20/20 split.

Observed citations are evaluation links. They are not treated as proof that one document
copied another. Perfect citation-link recovery mainly verifies metadata handling because
the citation itself is an input feature.

OpenAlex data is CC0. API responses are cached locally with their retrieval date.
See [OpenAlex API documentation](https://docs.openalex.org/how-to-use-the-api/api-overview).

## Acquisition

Review the manifests first. AVeriTeC is noncommercial.

```powershell
.\scripts\acquire_research_data.ps1 -AcceptResearchLicenses
```

The script checks exact SHA-256 hashes before extraction. Adapters themselves never
access the network.

## Leakage controls

- Claims, not individual documents, define stance train and validation partitions
- Test labels are used only after predictions are complete
- Oracle synthetic family identifiers are absent from `Document`
- Gold citation edges are isolated from model inputs
- Probability calibration uses validation predictions only
- Every method receives its own claim-probability calibrator

## What the data cannot establish

AVeriTeC does not provide gold copying families. OpenAlex provides citations, not copying
labels. The only exact copying lineage in this release is synthetic. Real-data results
therefore support calibration and citation-link conclusions, not a claim that natural
news genealogy has been solved.

documents.content:
# Reproducibility guide

## Environment

Use Python 3.11 or newer on a CPU. The default benchmark does not need a GPU, API key,
model checkpoint, or network connection after package installation.

```bash
python -m venv .venv
python -m pip install -e ".[dev]"
pytest -q
python -m lineagerag.cli smoke --seed 14 --out artifacts/smoke
python -m lineagerag.cli inspect-run artifacts/smoke
```

## Full research run

Review the external licenses before acquisition. AVeriTeC is noncommercial.

```powershell
.\scripts\acquire_research_data.ps1 -AcceptResearchLicenses

python -m lineagerag.cli train-lineage `
  --out models/dependency.json `
  --seed 14

python -m lineagerag.cli evaluate `
  --config configs/smoke.yaml `
  --lineage-model models/dependency.json `
  --out artifacts/synthetic-learned

python -m lineagerag.cli evaluate-real `
  --scifact-source data/external/scifact `
  --averitec-source data/external/averitec/AVeriTeC-7c62d1ec8df3fb560d6efe2b85fa191135636f81 `
  --lineage-model models/dependency.json `
  --out artifacts/real `
  --seed 14

python -m lineagerag.cli evaluate-citations `
  --scifact-source data/external/scifact `
  --lineage-model models/dependency.json `
  --cache data/external/openalex `
  --out artifacts/citations
```

The AVeriTeC extracted folder includes the pinned upstream commit in its name.

Raw data, normalized records, API caches, fitted models, and run artifacts are ignored.
Aggregate results under `reports` are tracked.

## Seed policy

`ExperimentConfig.seed` controls synthetic generation. NumPy uses an explicit local random
generator. SimHash uses BLAKE2b instead of Python's process-randomized hash.

Runs must report:

- package version
- configuration file
- seed
- claim and document counts
- data split or template allocation
- full artifact directory
- upstream data commit and checksum
- calibration split
- paired confidence interval for the kill criterion

## Artifact schemas

`claim_results.csv` has one row for each claim and method. It stores labels, probability,
raw counts, effective counts, family count, copy risk, false-corroboration event, and search
cost.

`predicted_edges.csv` stores claim ID, directed document pair, edge probability, and edge
type.

`predicted_families.csv` stores claim ID, document ID, and predicted family ID.

`trajectories.jsonl` stores active-search decisions in execution order.

`metrics.json` stores the full method summary and the synthetic kill-criterion sanity check.

## Adding a graph template

1. Add the name and a `TemplatePlan` in `synthetic/graph_templates.py`
2. Define family sizes, family stances, graph shapes, and the claim label
3. Add observed mutations without embedding a family label in `Document`
4. Add generator and no-leakage tests
5. Add the template to a configuration file

## Adding a real-data adapter

1. Require a user-supplied local path
2. Record data license and version outside generated metrics
3. Map raw fields into `ClaimSpec`, `Document`, and `EvidenceObservation`
4. Keep gold lineage and labels in separate evaluation files
5. Implement temporal train, validation, and test partitions
6. Fail with an actionable message if the source is missing

Adapters must not download or redistribute datasets automatically.

## Reading the genealogy

Fill color identifies the inferred family. Border color identifies support, refute, mixed,
or neutral stance. A diamond is an inferred root. Edge direction follows the estimated
publication path.

Compare raw sources with effective evidence before interpreting the posterior. A high raw
count and low effective count signals copy concentration.

documents.title: robustask — README.md
documents.content:
# RobustAsk

RobustAsk is an offline research framework for clarification when a user answer may be wrong.

Most clarification systems model a missing value and assume that asking reveals useful information. RobustAsk treats the answer as an observation from an uncertain channel. The controller estimates field values, user reliability, systematic confusion, and fatigue before it chooses whether to ask, rephrase, cross-check, use a deterministic verifier, act, or abstain.

The repository is designed for reproducible systems research. The default benchmark needs no API key, GPU, model download, or external dataset.

## Research status

This is a runnable research prototype with a paper scaffold. It is not presented as a completed paper result.

The built-in smoke run checks installation, policy behavior, metrics, plots, and artifact contracts. Its sample is intentionally small. A successful smoke criterion is evidence that the experiment is worth scaling, not evidence that the research claim is established.

The first frozen five-seed BookSafe study is reported in
[results/booksafe_5seed/README.md](results/booksafe_5seed/README.md). It
substantially reduced catastrophic errors in the configured synthetic test,
but missed the truthful-user non-inferiority margin. The recorded kill
criterion is therefore not met.

## What is implemented

- Exact discrete inference over task fields and terminal goals
- Beta reliability posteriors for each user-provided field
- Dirichlet-style categorical confusion counts
- A fatigue adjustment in reliability logit space
- Hard reliability updates after deterministic verification
- Fractional reliability updates when only user answers are available
- Robust value of sample information based on decision-risk reduction
- Typed actions for ask, rephrase, cross-check, tool, act, and abstain
- Six base user profiles and three held-out profile mixtures
- ToyLogic tasks with one, two, or three missing values
- BookSafe tasks with asymmetric and catastrophic parameter losses
- Eight comparison policies plus the RobustAsk controller
- Calibration, selective-risk, regret, burden, and bootstrap metrics
- Local adapters for Logic-Q style CSV and normalized clarification data
- Deterministic tests and a complete offline artifact pipeline

## Design boundary

The evaluator owns ground truth. A normal controller receives only:

- the public task schema
- priors and constraints
- observations emitted by an allowed interaction
- its current belief state
- the remaining interaction budget

It does not receive the simulator profile label, true field values, or oracle decision. Oracle policies are isolated by name and receive evaluator-only context that normal policies never see.

## Decision rule

For belief state $b$, the risk of stopping is

```math
R(b) = \min_d \mathbb{E}_{h \sim b}[L(d, h)]
```

For an information action $a$, RobustAsk scores a conservative decision-risk reduction

```math
\mathrm{RVSI}(a) =
\min_{\rho \in \mathcal{C}(b)}
\mathbb{E}_{o \mid a, \rho}
\left[R(b) - R(b^{a,o})\right]
- c_{\mathrm{burden}}(a)
- c_{\mathrm{tool}}(a)
```

$\mathcal{C}(b)$ is a small grid drawn from the current Beta credible interval. Deterministic verification uses an exact observation model. The implementation optimizes expected decision loss rather than raw entropy reduction.

## Install

Python 3.11 or newer is required.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/pxnkit/robustask.git
cd robustask
python -m venv .venv
```

Activate the environment on Linux or macOS:

```bash
source .venv/bin/activate
```

Activate it on Windows PowerShell:

```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
```

Install the project:

```bash
pip install -e ".[dev]"
```

## Run the offline smoke benchmark

```bash
python -m robustask.cli smoke --seed 13 --out artifacts/smoke
python -m robustask.cli inspect-run artifacts/smoke
```

The smoke command generates 100 tasks, evaluates six profiles and five policies, writes every required artifact, and fails if an artifact is missing. All nine policy implementations remain available to focused experiment configurations.

Expected files:

```text
artifacts/smoke/
  metrics.json
  metrics_by_profile.csv
  trajectories.jsonl
  calibration.csv
  summary.md
  catastrophic_error_by_profile.png
```

## Run focused experiments

```bash
python -m robustask.cli evaluate --config configs/toylogic.yaml --out artifacts/toylogic
python -m robustask.cli evaluate --config configs/booksafe.yaml --out artifacts/booksafe
```

Run the frozen five-seed BookSafe study:

```bash
python -m robustask.cli study-booksafe --config configs/booksafe_5seed.yaml --out artifacts/booksafe_5seed
python -m robustask.cli inspect-study artifacts/booksafe_5seed
```

This protocol compares all nine policies on 100 BookSafe tasks per seed. It
evaluates the three held-out profile mixtures plus a truthful control. The
runner writes a SHA-256 digest of the complete configuration before the first
evaluation starts, then reports seed-level metrics and paired bootstrap
intervals.

Prepare a local Logic-Q style dataset:

```bash
python -m robustask.cli prepare questbench --source PATH --out data/questbench
```

If the path has no recognized CSV, the adapter writes a manifest that clearly labels the generated fallback. It never downloads data unless download behavior is explicitly requested. Automatic download is not implemented in this release.

## Benchmarks

### ToyLogic

ToyLogic generates boolean constraint problems whose answer is a public function of one to three hidden fields. The benchmark isolates sequential acquisition behavior while keeping exact inference cheap enough for unit tests.

### BookSafe

BookSafe generates booking, refund, account update, medical intake, and form submission tasks. A wrong critical value can create catastrophic loss. Some fields support a deterministic verifier with a stated cost.

The tasks are synthetic. They are not operational medical, financial, or account-management systems.

## Simulated user channels

Base profiles:

- truthful
- unsure
- contradictory
- systematically mistaken
- overconfident
- fatigued

Held-out mixtures:

- fatigued and overconfident
- unsure and systematic
- contradictory and fatigued

Profile parameters live in YAML. Each episode receives a stable seed derived from the run seed, task identifier, profile, and policy.

## Policies

- `ActImmediatelyBaseline`
- `AskAllBaseline`
- `AskOnceMostUncertainBaseline`
- `EntropyGainTruthfulBaseline`
- `EVPIWithoutReliabilityBaseline`
- `StaticReliabilityBayesBaseline`
- `OracleReliabilityPolicy`
- `OracleFullInformationPolicy`
- `RobustAskController`

Every policy runs through the same simulator, belief boundary, loss function, and metric writer.

## Metrics

The evaluator reports:

- task success
- catastrophic error rate
- expected utility
- mean and median question count
- tool count and interaction burden
- abstention rate, precision, and recall
- regret against both oracle policies
- Brier score and negative log likelihood
- expected calibration error
- selective risk at multiple coverage levels
- per-profile breakdowns
- paired bootstrap confidence intervals

The summary evaluates the configured smoke kill criterion at a matched question budget. It also states whether the sample is statistically conclusive.

## Reproducibility

All stochastic components use explicit NumPy generators or stable derived seeds. Run configuration, seed, elapsed time, task count, and external-data status are recorded in `metrics.json`.

See [docs/reproducibility.md](docs/reproducibility.md) for extension instructions and artifact details.

## Scope and attribution

This repository does not claim to introduce clarification, value of information, false-premise correction, structured tool uncertainty, or user simulation. Its target is narrower: decisions under uncertain and changing answer reliability.

All code and built-in synthetic data in this repository were created for RobustAsk. External papers, datasets, figures, archives, and reference implementations are not bundled, copied, or required for the offline benchmark. Prior research is discussed as prior research in [paper/related_work.md](paper/related_work.md).

## Current limitations

- The task state is small and discrete
- Field posteriors are factorized before the public goal mapping
- Reliability and truth can be weakly identifiable without verification
- The fatigue model is intentionally simple
- Synthetic profiles are not validated against human interactions
- The optional language model backend renders actions but does not train a model
- The smoke benchmark is too small for a publication claim

## License

MIT

documents.content:
# RobustAsk synthetic benchmark card

## Summary

RobustAsk includes two generated benchmark families for testing clarification under answer-channel uncertainty.

ToyLogic contains small boolean constraint tasks with one to three unavailable values.

BookSafe contains synthetic parameterized actions for booking, refund, account update, medical intake, and form submission scenarios. Critical parameter errors receive a larger loss.

## Data generation

Tasks are generated locally from explicit domains and seeded NumPy random generators. Every task has:

- a controller-visible `TaskSpec`
- an evaluator-only `HiddenState`
- a public mapping from complete assignments to terminal decisions
- an explicit loss matrix

No external dataset is required or downloaded.

## User channels

Profiles are parameterized observation channels. They control accuracy, uncertainty, contradiction, confidence, fatigue, and categorical confusion. Held-out mixtures combine mechanisms that are not used for threshold tuning.

## Intended use

- controller development
- regression tests for belief updates
- safety-oriented policy comparisons
- calibration and selective-risk experiments

## Out-of-scope use

- medical decision support
- financial transactions
- real account updates
- claims about human behavior without validation
- ranking or judging individual users

## Known limitations

The language is templated. Field domains are small. Profiles are synthetic. The benchmark does not capture social context, strategic deception, accessibility needs, cultural variation, or natural conversational repair.

## Optional adapters

The Logic-Q style adapter reads a local CSV when a recognized answer column is available. If parsing is impossible, it writes a manifest that labels generated fallback data. The structured clarification adapter expects normalized `TaskInstance` JSONL and raises a clear error when data is absent.

documents.title: robustask — docs/model_card.md
documents.content:
# RobustAsk controller card

## Model details

RobustAsk is a deterministic Bayesian decision controller. It is not a pretrained language model.

It maintains:

- categorical posteriors over fields
- a posterior over terminal goals
- Beta reliability parameters per field
- categorical confusion counts
- a simple fatigue state
- a full observation log

## Inputs

- public task schema
- constraints and priors
- allowed observations
- interaction budget

## Outputs

One typed action:

- ask
- rephrase
- cross-check
- tool
- act
- abstain

## Objective

The controller minimizes posterior expected terminal loss. Information actions are selected by conservative expected risk reduction over a small reliability credible set, less burden and tool cost.

## Safety properties

- simulator truth is outside the controller schema
- deterministic verification is explicitly costed
- abstention is available when residual risk is high
- every random component is seeded
- trajectories expose the controller's belief before and after observations

## Limitations

Exact enumeration scales poorly with many fields. Reliability priors affect behavior. Fractional reliability learning is not identifiable without additional assumptions. The fatigue model is not fitted to human data. The controller does not parse free-form language.

documents.content:
# Reproducibility guide

## Environment

Use Python 3.11 or newer on CPU.

```bash
python -m venv .venv
```

Linux or macOS:

```bash
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -e ".[dev]"
```

Windows PowerShell:

```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
pip install -e ".[dev]"
```

## Acceptance commands

```bash
pytest -q
python -m robustask.cli smoke --seed 13 --out artifacts/smoke
python -m robustask.cli inspect-run artifacts/smoke
```

## Focused runs

```bash
python -m robustask.cli evaluate --config configs/toylogic.yaml --out artifacts/toylogic
python -m robustask.cli evaluate --config configs/booksafe.yaml --out artifacts/booksafe
```

## Seed policy

The run seed initializes process-level Python and NumPy generators. Episode seeds are derived with BLAKE2s from:

- run seed
- task identifier
- profile name
- policy name

Python's process-randomized `hash` function is not used.

## Artifact format

`metrics.json` contains run metadata, aggregate policy metrics, selective risk, oracle regret, and the kill-criterion calculation.

`metrics_by_profile.csv` contains policy and profile slices.

`trajectories.jsonl` records actions, allowed observations, posterior risk, and goal beliefs.

`calibration.csv` contains binned field-confidence calibration.

`summary.md` is a human-readable report.

`catastrophic_error_by_profile.png` compares selected policies.

## Add a user profile

1. Add a parameter mapping in `robustask/simulators.py`
2. Add the same profile parameters to the experiment YAML when tuning them
3. Add the profile name to the configured profile list
4. Mark it as held out only if thresholds were not tuned on it
5. Add a deterministic profile test

The simulator may use the private profile name. Observations must never contain it.

## Add a benchmark

1. Generate `TaskInstance` values with public `TaskSpec` and private `HiddenState`
2. Define a complete goal table over public field domains
3. Define terminal actions and an explicit loss matrix
4. Mark critical fields and optional verifiers
5. Add the generator to `build_tasks`
6. Add a small test for inference and loss behavior
7. Document whether data is generated, local, or downloaded

## External data policy

The required benchmark never downloads external data. Optional adapters take explicit local paths. A missing path must produce either a labeled generated fallback or a clear error.

documents.title: skillfalsify — README.md
documents.content:
FALSIFY

Active minimal-counterexample discovery for selective procedural memory

Quick start · What runs · Architecture · Originality · API · Research status

FALSIFY tests a learned agent procedure before trusting it on a similar task. It searches a typed neighborhood around the source task, executes each legal mutation in a deterministic sandbox, measures the procedure against a contract-aware fallback, minimizes harmful cases, and learns a calibrated deployment gate. The default path runs offline on CPU. It does not need an API key, a GPU, a model server, a live database, or a private benchmark. ## Why this project exists Successful experience is useful evidence, but it is not a general safety argument. A procedure that worked yesterday may fail after a tool disappears, an argument changes, confirmation becomes mandatory, a read turns stale, or a side effect becomes destructive. FALSIFY treats procedural memory as a policy with a measurable boundary. The system asks three practical questions: 1. Does the procedure help compared with the same agent without that procedure 2. What is the smallest legal task change that makes reuse harmful 3. Is the estimated negative-transfer risk low enough to use the procedure now ## Quick start Requirements: - Python 3.11 or newer - Node.js 22 or newer - Docker is optional ```bash python -m venv .venv source .venv/bin/activate python scripts/task.py setup python scripts/task.py smoke ``` On Windows: ```powershell python -m venv .venv .\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1 python scripts\task.py setup python scripts\task.py smoke ``` Build the dashboard and start the combined application: ```bash cd apps/web npm run build cd ../.. python -m skillfalsify api ``` Open `http://127.0.0.1:8000`. ## What runs `make smoke` or `python scripts/task.py smoke` performs a genuine vertical slice: 1. Compile a typed synthetic task contract 2. Execute a successful source trajectory 3. Extract a versioned procedure from observable actions 4. Generate legal and invalid mutation programs 5. Reject unsatisfiable tasks before execution 6. Run paired control and treatment branches with matched seeds 7. Replay both branches and compare exact fingerprints 8. Discover harmful procedure reuse 9. Reduce one failure to a locally minimal counterexample 10. Train a CPU applicability model 11. Calibrate a finite-sample selective threshold 12. Use the procedure on a compatible neighbor 13. Fall back on the minimized counterexample 14. Export metrics, traces, plots, a certificate, and a run manifest The demo never returns a stored trace in place of execution. ## Architecture ![FALSIFY execution loop](reports/generated/architecture.svg) | Layer | Responsibility | |---|---| | Procedure registry | Versioned procedure steps, schemas, evidence links, lifecycle, and known failures | | Contract compiler | Tool schemas, state, constraints, success checks, hidden fields, and fail-closed validation | | Mutation registry | Typed transforms with preconditions, legality checks, distance, cost, and rollback | | Deterministic sandbox | Copy-on-write state, registered fixture tools, state hashes, call logs, and exact resets | | Paired effects | Matched control and treatment execution with explicit direct-effect labels | | Active search | Random, coverage, uncertainty, bandit, evolutionary, and combined acquisition policies | | Minimization | Greedy delta debugging with legality, solvability, replay, and stable-harm checks | | Applicability | Procedure-specific logistic risk model and expected-effect head | | Calibration | Platt scaling, isotonic calibration, and registered finite-sample risk control | | Controller | Hard contract checks, shift detection, risk gating, fallback, and abstention | | Ledger | Append-only SQLite events protected by a verifiable SHA-256 hash chain | The sandbox is an interpreter for registered tools. It does not evaluate generated Python, spawn processes, read host files, or enable network access. ## MiniSkillFalsify The bundled benchmark is synthetic and deterministic. Its source task resolves a ticket while preserving notes and unrelated state. Registered mutations cover: - Missing and distractor tools - Renamed arguments, changed types, and changed enums - New confirmation and authentication requirements - Ordering changes and stale reads - Destructive, collateral, irreversible, and delayed side effects - Environment version changes - Tight execution budgets - Both-branches-fail cases - Invalid unsatisfiable tasks Every descendant of a source task stays in its assigned train or calibration group. ## Commands | Command | Purpose | |---|---| | `make setup` | Install Python and web dependencies | | `make lint` | Run Ruff | | `make typecheck` | Run mypy and TypeScript checks | | `make test` | Run Python and web tests | | `make test-mutations` | Verify mutation legality and reproducibility | | `make test-sandbox` | Verify reset, limits, failures, and isolation | | `make test-replay` | Verify paired effects and exact replay | | `make test-calibration` | Verify model and calibration behavior | | `make test-concurrency` | Verify state isolation under concurrent runs | | `make smoke` | Execute the complete offline vertical slice | | `make benchmark-small` | Compare search policies under one budget | | `make paper-smoke` | Regenerate paper inputs from a completed run | | `make demo` | Generate verified demo data | | `make docker-up` | Build and run the production container | | `make docker-test` | Run tests inside the container | | `make reproduce-mini` | Rebuild all bundled benchmark artifacts | Use `make.cmd ` on Windows if GNU Make is unavailable. ## API The same routes are available at the root and under `/api/v1`. | Method | Route | Purpose | |---|---|---| | `POST` | `/procedures/extract` | Extract a procedure from a clean trace | | `GET` | `/procedures` | List registered procedures | | `GET` | `/procedures/{id}` | Inspect procedure evidence and contracts | | `POST` | `/tasks/compile` | Validate and compile a task | | `GET` | `/mutations/operators` | Inspect the mutation registry | | `POST` | `/mutations/propose` | Produce an idempotent typed mutation | | `POST` | `/experiments/paired-run` | Run matched control and treatment branches | | `POST` | `/counterexamples/minimize` | Reduce a harmful mutation program | | `GET` | `/counterexamples` | List certified counterexamples | | `POST` | `/models/train-applicability` | Train the CPU risk model | | `POST` | `/models/calibrate` | Fit the registered selective threshold | | `POST` | `/controller/decide` | Use, fall back, clarify, or abstain | | `GET` | `/experiments/{id}` | Inspect observable traces and state changes | | `GET` | `/reports/latest` | Read the latest completed run | | `GET` | `/health` | Check API, ledger, and sandbox status | Mutation writes require an idempotency key. Request bodies are bounded to 1 MB. Error responses carry stable machine-readable codes. ## Verified mini run The committed report was produced by `python -m skillfalsify smoke --seed 17`. | Metric | Observed value | |---|---:| | Valid paired executions | 96 | | Valid full-search executions | 17 | | Full-search counterexamples | 12 | | Unique full-search failure families | 6 | | Applicability AUROC | 1.000 | | Applicability AUPRC | 1.000 | | Brier score | 0.011 | | Negative transfer before gating | 0.800 | | Negative transfer after gating | 0.000 | | Procedure-use coverage | 0.200 | | External model calls | 0 | | GPU seconds | 0 | These values describe one small synthetic benchmark. The perfect ranking score is not evidence of broad generalization. The benchmark is deliberately separable so the repository can verify the entire execution and calibration path offline. ## Originality and research boundaries The implementation, synthetic benchmark, dashboard, tests, documentation, and generated experiment artifacts were created for this repository. Background reading helped define the broad research question. Supplied reference files are not included, quoted, reproduced, summarized as original work, or used as experimental evidence. No external repository code, private benchmark records, published result tables, or paper figures are redistributed here. External benchmark names describe optional adapter boundaries only. The repository reports no results for an external benchmark and makes no comparison claim against published work. See [docs/originality-and-source-boundaries.md](docs/originality-and-source-boundaries.md) for the full public boundary statement. ## Research status Implemented and exercised: - Typed contracts and procedures - Eighteen mutation operators - Deterministic paired execution and exact replay - Active search and bounded neighborhood enumeration - Counterexample certification and local minimization - CPU risk learning and calibration - Selective deployment decisions - FastAPI and React applications - Security guards, CI, Docker, and reproducibility artifacts Configured but not executed: - AppWorld - BFCL v3 - BFCL v4 - ALFWorld - EvoAgentBench - Open-model applicability judges - GPU experiments The repository does not claim that active search beats a strong judge on unseen operator families. That claim remains behind the registered kill criterion and needs matched-cost experiments on public environments. ## Repository layout ```text apps/api deployment entrypoint apps/web React and TypeScript workbench src/skillfalsify research and runtime package data/mini_skillfalsify synthetic offline benchmark configs versioned experiment and policy settings tests unit, integration, security, and concurrency tests docs architecture, estimands, threat model, and protocol paper publication skeleton reports/generated artifacts produced by verified runs third_party adapter boundary and dependency policy ``` ## Security and privacy Trajectories and procedure text are treated as untrusted data. The project includes secret redaction, display escaping, scoped path resolution, archive traversal checks, request limits, append-only provenance, network-off sandbox defaults, non-root containers, and no-new-privileges runtime settings. Only observable messages, actions, tool calls, observations, state changes, and structured reason codes are stored. Hidden model reasoning is not collected. See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) and [docs/threat-model.md](docs/threat-model.md). ## Reproducibility Each run writes: - Contract, procedure, model, registry, and certificate hashes - Python and platform versions - Seed and benchmark version - Accepted and rejected proposals - Control and treatment traces - Replay fingerprints - Calibration scope and availability - Complete branch, model-call, and GPU cost counts Start with [docs/reproducibility.md](docs/reproducibility.md). ## License Code is released under the MIT License. The synthetic MiniSkillFalsify data is released under CC0-1.0.

documents.title: skillfalsify — docs/architecture.md
documents.content:
# Architecture

FALSIFY is an offline-first research system for finding where a learned tool-use procedure becomes harmful.

## Execution boundary

The trusted runtime contains the contract compiler, registered mutation operators, deterministic fixture tools, outcome checks, and artifact writers. Model text, trajectories, procedure records, task contracts, and imported manifests are untrusted inputs.

The sandbox accepts structured actions only. A call names a registered tool and supplies arguments that must pass its current schema. No input can inject source code into the runtime.

## Main data flow

1. A successful observable trajectory is converted into a typed procedure
2. The source task is compiled into tools, state, constraints, and exact checks
3. A search policy selects typed mutation programs
4. The compiler rejects invalid or unsatisfiable descendants
5. Legal descendants run through matched control and treatment branches
6. Exact replay validates that the intervention label is stable
7. Harmful cases enter the minimizer
8. Safe and harmful examples train a procedure-specific risk model
9. A held-out calibration group defines the selective threshold
10. The controller requires contract compatibility and acceptable risk

## State and replay

Each branch starts from an independent deep copy of the compiled initial state. Every tool call produces:

- Action and validated arguments
- Observation code and bounded payload
- State hash before the call
- State hash after the call
- Top-level state diff
- Recorded side effects
- Hard constraint violations

No-op replay executes the same action list from the same initial state and seed. The run is valid only when the trace fingerprint, initial hash, final hash, outcome, and cost match.

## Append-only ledger

Experiment events are stored in SQLite. Update and delete triggers reject mutation of existing rows. Every event includes the previous event hash, which creates a verifiable chain over ordered canonical JSON records.

## Deployment controller

The controller fails closed. It blocks procedure use when:

- A permitted tool is missing
- A used schema changed
- The procedure omits a new confirmation or authentication step
- The procedure can act on stale state
- A used tool has a forbidden side effect
- The environment version shifted
- A known counterexample dominates the task
- Calibration support is insufficient
- Predicted risk exceeds the registered threshold

An environment shift disables the old calibration guarantee. The default response is abstention.

| BFCL v3 | Unavailable until installed and pinned | Function sets, schemas, serial order, multi-turn state, and responses |
| BFCL v4 | Unavailable until installed and pinned | Reported separately from v3 |

documents.title: skillfalsify — docs/estimands.md
documents.content:
# Estimands and labels

## Direct procedure effect

For task contract `x`, procedure `p`, and matched seed `u`, define:

```text
effect(p, x, u) = utility(treatment) - utility(control)
```

The control branch uses the contract-aware general agent. The treatment branch executes the frozen procedure. Both branches use the same compiled task, initial state, environment version, seed, and resource limits.

Utility combines exact task success, hard violations, execution cost, and a fixed planning overhead. The overhead is versioned and identical across runs in one experiment.

## Negative transfer

A procedure causes negative transfer when the control branch reaches the goal and treatment either:

- Lowers utility beyond the registered margin
- Violates a hard contract
- Becomes unexecutable because a required tool or schema changed

Both-branches-fail and environment-failure cases are not procedure counterexamples.

## Minimum counterexample

A certified counterexample must be legal, solvable, replay-valid, and harmful. Minimization removes registered operators while preserving those conditions.

The implementation claims local minimality under the registered mutation grammar. It does not claim global minimality over natural-language tasks.

## Selective deployment

Coverage is the fraction of evaluated descendants on which the gate uses the procedure. Selective risk is the negative-transfer rate among those accepted descendants.

The finite-sample risk bound applies only to the registered exchangeable operator mixture. Operator holdout and environment shift are empirical OOD evaluations without the same guarantee.

documents.title: skillfalsify — docs/originality-and-source-boundaries.md
documents.content:
# Originality and source boundaries

The implementation, synthetic benchmark, UI, documentation, tests, and generated experiment artifacts in this repository were authored for FALSIFY.

## Development inputs

Background reading was used only to identify the broad problem of deciding when a reusable agent procedure stops being safe or useful.

Supplied reference files are not included in the repository. Their prose, code, figures, tables, benchmark records, and reported results were not copied into the implementation or presented as FALSIFY outputs.

No external repository code, private benchmark records, model outputs, result tables, or paper figures are redistributed here.

## Repository-owned work

The following material was created specifically for this repository:

- The typed task and procedure schemas
- The deterministic MiniSkillFalsify fixture and its records
- The mutation registry and legality checks
- The paired execution, replay, search, minimization, calibration, and controller code
- The API, command line interface, dashboard, tests, reports, and documentation
- The generated branding image and architecture diagram

## Third-party boundaries

Runtime and development libraries are declared through standard Python and npm package metadata. Their code is not vendored as original work.

Optional public benchmark support is implemented through narrow adapters. Users install those dependencies separately and retain responsibility for their licenses and data terms.

External benchmark names identify compatibility targets only. No external dataset was downloaded, copied, or executed for the bundled results.

## Claims policy

The project does not claim ownership of general ideas such as procedural memory, paired evaluation, active testing, counterexample minimization, or selective prediction.

The reported measurements apply only to the versioned synthetic fixture and registered mutation mixture. The project does not claim external benchmark performance, superiority over published systems, or general safety for arbitrary agents.

documents.title: skillfalsify — docs/reproducibility.md
documents.content:
# Reproducibility protocol

## Deterministic path

Run:

```bash
python scripts/task.py reproduce-mini
```

This regenerates the smoke run, policy comparison, calibration artifacts, plots, certificate, report, and paper table with seed 17.

## Expected outputs

`reports/generated` contains:

- `latest.json`
- `metrics.json`
- `predictions.jsonl`
- `predictions.csv`
- `counterexample-certificate.json`
- `applicability-model.json`
- `calibration.json`
- `risk-coverage.svg`
- `applicability-map.svg`
- `architecture.svg`
- `reproducibility-manifest.json`
- `report.md`
- `mini-results.tex`

## Split discipline

MiniSkillFalsify uses six independent source-task instances. Instances 0 through 3 train the model. Instances 4 and 5 form the calibration group. All descendants of one source task remain in the same group.

The committed smoke run does not use the registered operator holdout as evidence for a conformal guarantee. Held-out operators must be reported as empirical OOD performance.

## Cost accounting

The manifest counts:

- All proposed mutations
- Invalid compiler rejections
- Valid paired executions
- Replay branches
- Model calls
- GPU time

The default path records zero model calls and zero GPU time.

## Clean verification

```bash
python scripts/task.py lint
python scripts/task.py typecheck
python scripts/task.py test
python scripts/task.py reproduce-mini
```

The run ID is content-derived from the seed, procedure, certificate, and trained model.

documents.title: regimebank — README.md
documents.content:
# RegimeBank

RegimeBank gives a lifelong agent separate memories for operating regimes that can disappear and
later return.

Most memory policies assume that recent experience is always the most relevant. That assumption
breaks on streams such as API v1, API v2, then API v1 again. A sliding window must relearn the
first API. A global memory can mix incompatible procedures. RegimeBank detects the change, keeps
the memories separate, and reactivates the earlier bank when the first regime returns.

The repository is runnable on a laptop. It includes a recurring contextual-bandit benchmark,
Bayesian online change-point detection, regime-aware memory, six baselines, an oracle, metrics,
plots, tests, and a JSONL adapter for real agent traces.

![Benchmark output](artifacts/demo/benchmark.png)

## What is implemented

- Bayesian online change-point detection with a multivariate Student-t predictive model
- Episodic memory for concrete task, action, and outcome records
- Procedural memory with one regularized reward model per action
- An invariant pool for action evidence validated in more than one regime
- Regime reactivation from learned signal prototypes
- Posterior-weighted retrieval when regime identity is uncertain
- Bank merging only after validation succeeds in both directions
- Abrupt, gradual, cyclic, and recurring schedules
- API, tool-schema, and hidden-transition synthetic domains
- Global, sliding-window, reservoir, periodic-deletion, exponential-decay, and oracle baselines
- Prequential and recurrence-focused evaluation
- Reproducible CSV, JSON, and PNG artifacts

## Quick start

RegimeBank requires Python 3.11 or newer.

```bash
python -m venv .venv

# Windows
.venv\Scripts\activate

# macOS and Linux
source .venv/bin/activate

python -m pip install -e ".[dev]"
regimebank run --config configs/aba.toml --output artifacts/latest
```

For a short smoke test:

```bash
regimebank run --config configs/aba.toml --output artifacts/quick --quick
```

The command writes:

```text
artifacts/latest/
  benchmark.png
  metrics_by_run.csv
  metrics_summary.csv
  summary.json
  trace.csv
```

## Expected behavior

The default schedule has three equal segments:

```text
alpha -> beta -> alpha
```

The first boundary is a new regime. The second boundary is a recurrence. RegimeBank should create a
new bank at the first boundary and reactivate the original alpha bank at the second boundary.

The benchmark is useful when these conditions hold:

1. RegimeBank recovers faster on the returning alpha segment than a sliding window or periodic
   deletion policy
2. Alpha memories do not dominate decisions during beta
3. Dynamic regret remains below the global-memory baseline
4. Change alarms stay close to true boundaries

Treat these as behavioral checks, not guaranteed research conclusions. Results depend on the
schedule, seed set, memory capacity, and detector settings.

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["Streaming task signals"] --> B["Bayesian change detector"]
    B --> C["Regime posterior"]
    C --> D["Episodic banks"]
    C --> E["Procedural banks"]
    D --> F["Posterior-weighted retrieval"]
    E --> F
    G["Invariant memory"] --> F
    F --> H["Action scores"]
    H --> I["Outcome feedback"]
    I --> A
    I --> D
    I --> E
    I --> G
```

Each detector signal contains:

```text
tool-schema fingerprint
task embedding
previous outcome
transition prediction error
memory agreement
```

The synthetic environment produces all five signals. A real agent can provide the same normalized
event shape through the JSONL adapter.

## Memory routing

At every step, the agent updates the run-length posterior. A detected change triggers one of two
paths:

1. Reactivate an existing bank when its signal prototype receives enough posterior mass
2. Create a new bank when no previous regime is a credible match

Retrieval remains weighted across banks while the posterior is uncertain. The system does not force
an early hard assignment.

Bank merging is conservative. Two inactive banks merge only when prototype similarity is high and
each procedural model predicts the other bank's held-out episodes with sufficient accuracy.

See [docs/design.md](docs/design.md) for the model and implementation details.

## Benchmark configurations

| Config | Domain | Schedule | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `configs/aba.toml` | API | Abrupt A-B-A | Main recurrence test |
| `configs/gradual.toml` | API and dynamics | Gradual A-B-A | Slow adaptation test |
| `configs/transition.toml` | Hidden transition | Abrupt A-B-A | Outcome-driven detection |

All environments are synthetic and generated locally. No external benchmark data is distributed.

## Metrics

The runner reports:

- Prequential success
- Mean reward
- Dynamic regret
- Change-detection delay
- False alarms
- Recovery time
- Recurrence gain
- Backward transfer
- Forward transfer
- Post-hoc regime identification accuracy
- Mean and final storage
- Retrieval token proxy

Metrics are calculated for every seed and then aggregated with the standard error.

## Use real agent traces

Export one JSON object per line:

```json
{
  "step": 0,
  "task_embedding": [0.21, -0.08, 0.44],
  "tool_schema": {"name": "lookup", "arguments": {"query": "string"}},
  "outcome": 1.0,
  "transition_error": 0.05,
  "memory_agreement": 0.91,
  "metadata": {"request_id": "local-0001"}
}
```

Validate the stream before integrating it:

```bash
regimebank validate-stream examples/events.jsonl
```

Tool schemas are canonicalized before hashing, so key order does not change the fingerprint.
Embeddings must have a consistent dimension across the stream.

## Python API

```python
from regimebank import ExperimentConfig, run_experiment

config = ExperimentConfig.from_toml("configs/aba.toml")
result = run_experiment(config, "artifacts/latest")

for row in result.aggregate_metrics:
    print(row["agent"], row["prequential_success_mean"])
```

## Development

```bash
python -m pip install -e ".[dev]"
pytest
ruff check .
```

The test suite covers detector normalization, abrupt shift detection, recurrence reactivation,
canonical schema fingerprints, JSONL validation, and the full artifact pipeline.

## Scope

This release is an engineering reference for recurrence-aware memory. It is not a production policy
for autonomous decisions and it does not include integrations that require redistribution of
third-party code or datasets.

The adapter boundary is intentionally small. Connectors for larger agent systems can translate
their traces into `StreamEvent` without changing the detector or memory implementation.

## Provenance and license

The repository contains only original implementation code and generated synthetic outputs. It does
not package source papers, third-party archives, figures, or datasets. See
[NOTICE.md](NOTICE.md) for the provenance statement.

RegimeBank is available under the [MIT License](LICENSE).

documents.title: regimebank — docs/design.md
documents.content:
# RegimeBank design

## Goal

RegimeBank handles streams where an operating regime can disappear and later return. It separates
change detection from regime recognition:

- Change detection asks whether the current generating process changed
- Regime recognition asks whether the new process matches a bank seen before

That distinction is the core design decision.

## Signal model

At step \(t\), the detector receives:

\[
x_t = [s_t, e_t, d_t, o_{t-1}, \epsilon_{t-1}, a_{t-1}]
\]

where:

- \(s_t\) is the tool-schema fingerprint
- \(e_t\) is the task embedding
- \(d_t\) is the current transition-error signature
- \(o_{t-1}\) is the previous outcome
- \(\epsilon_{t-1}\) is the previous prediction error
- \(a_{t-1}\) is memory agreement

The reference environment scales stable schema features more strongly than task context. This makes
visible API changes easy to identify while preserving outcome-based evidence for hidden transition
changes.

## Bayesian online change-point detection

The detector maintains a posterior over run length:

\[
p(r_t \mid x_{1:t})
\]

Every run length has an independent Normal-Inverse-Gamma model per signal dimension. Integrating
the unknown mean and variance gives a Student-t predictive density. A constant hazard controls the
prior probability of a boundary.

The implementation truncates run length to a configurable maximum. This bounds memory and update
cost without changing the public interface.

## Regime recognition

Every bank stores an online signal prototype. After a detected change, RegimeBank compares the new
signal with all inactive prototypes.

The posterior combines prototype distance and a small usage prior. If no inactive bank clears the
reactivation threshold, the manager creates a new bank.

The current bank does not compete in the reactivation decision. A detected change cannot be
silently absorbed back into the same bank.

## Episodic memory

An episode stores:

- Context
- Action
- Observed reward
- Detector signal
- Stream step
- Utility
- Retrieval count

Retrieval uses squared Euclidean distance in normalized context space. A bounded bank retains
higher-utility and repeatedly useful episodes.

## Procedural memory

Each bank maintains a regularized linear reward model for every action:

\[
\hat{\theta}_a = A_a^{-1} b_a
\]

with:

\[
A_a = \lambda I + \sum_i x_i x_i^T
\]

\[
b_a = \sum_i r_i x_i
\]

Procedural and episodic predictions are blended. The procedural weight increases as a bank gains
experience.

## Invariant memory

The invariant pool tracks action evidence by bank. An action prior becomes invariant only after it
has enough observations in at least two regimes and each validated regime has non-trivial success.

The invariant contribution is deliberately small. It supports transfer without overriding
regime-specific procedures.

## Posterior-weighted retrieval

When the regime posterior is diffuse, RegimeBank queries every candidate bank and combines action
scores using posterior mass. This avoids a brittle early switch.

Once one bank dominates, the same equation naturally behaves like hard routing.

## Merge guard

Two inactive banks can merge only when all conditions hold:

1. Their signal prototypes are sufficiently similar
2. The left bank predicts the right bank's held-out episodes well
3. The right bank predicts the left bank's held-out episodes well

Validation in one direction is not enough.

## Complexity

Let \(R\) be the run-length cap, \(d\) the signal dimension, \(B\) the number of banks, and \(K\)
the retrieval count.

- Detector update is \(O(Rd)\)
- Regime scoring is \(O(Bd)\)
- Procedural prediction is \(O(Ad_c^3)\) with small context dimension \(d_c\)
- Episodic retrieval is linear in bank capacity in this reference implementation

Approximate nearest-neighbor retrieval can replace the linear scan without changing the manager.

documents.title: memintervene — README.md
documents.content:
# MemIntervene

**Replay-defined credit assignment for memory lifecycle operations in long-horizon agents.**

MemIntervene is an offline-first research and engineering system for answering a narrow question:
which memory record, representation, link, or lifecycle operation changed a later agent decision?
It treats credit as a paired intervention over a versioned memory state—not as retrieval frequency,
attention, citation, or terminal reward alone.

The repository is a complete deterministic vertical slice: immutable event ledger, rebuildable memory
views, typed interventions, four replay modes, exact effects, controlled-direct and total-system
estimands, Shapley and interaction diagnostics, a calibrated effect predictor, a conservative
fixed-budget policy, FastAPI, React/TypeScript replay console, tests, Docker, CI, and generated paper
assets. Python dependencies are resolved in `requirements.lock`; web dependencies and approved build
scripts are frozen in `apps/web/pnpm-lock.yaml` and `pnpm-workspace.yaml`.

> Research status: the software path is complete and verified; the current MiniMemIntervene run is a
> smoke-scale result, not a publication claim. The learned policy ties the strongest fixed baseline
> on the held-out synthetic split, so the policy kill criterion is not met.

## Why this project exists

Long-horizon memory systems can fail in ways that retrieval-only evaluation misses:

- a retrieved record may be redundant and have no marginal effect;
- an unretrieved record can displace the decisive record from top-k;
- a summary can drop a number or remove harmful noise;
- a stale preference or stored instruction can reverse an action;
- two memories can be useful only as a coalition;
- a link can enable multi-hop reasoning or create a false association.

Fine-Mem motivates fine-grained operation feedback; MemoryArena motivates action-coupled,
multi-session evaluation. MemIntervene takes inspiration from those research problems while using an
original ledger, intervention, replay, benchmark, policy, API, and interface. The reference PDFs are
not copied into this repository and `*.pdf` is ignored.

## System overview

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Observations, actions, tools] --> B[(Hash-chained event ledger)]
    B --> C[Deterministic materializer]
    C --> D[Versioned memory + lineage DAG]
    D --> E[Typed intervention]
    D --> F[Factual replay]
    E --> G[Counterfactual replay]
    F --> H[Paired effect]
    G --> H
    H --> I[Effect model + calibration]
    I --> J[Conservative budgeted policy]
    B --> K[FastAPI + React replay console]
    D --> K
    H --> K
```

Core invariants:

1. Raw source events are immutable. SQLite triggers reject `UPDATE` and `DELETE`.
2. Every branch is ordered, parent-linked, and hash-chained.
3. Memory views are deterministic functions of ledger history.
4. Derived records preserve source and parent lineage.
5. Forgetting and quarantine affect the active view but remain reversible in the research ledger.
6. Controlled-direct and total-system effects are never combined without labels.
7. Invalid or off-manifold replay is typed and excluded rather than silently scored.
8. The default action path never reads the benchmark's correct answer; only the environment scores it.

See [architecture](docs/architecture.md), [replay protocol](docs/replay-protocol.md), and
[reproducibility](docs/reproducibility.md).

## Quick start

Requirements: Python 3.12, Node.js 24, pnpm 11.9, and optionally GNU Make or Docker.

### Linux or macOS

```bash
make setup
make reproduce-mini
make demo
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:8000`. The API documentation is at `/api/docs`.

### Windows PowerShell

```powershell
.\make.cmd setup
.\make.cmd reproduce-mini
.\make.cmd demo
```

If Python is not on `PATH`, point the bootstrapper at it:

```powershell
$env:MEMINTERVENE_PYTHON = "C:\path\to\python.exe"
.\make.cmd setup
```

After dependency installation, the default dataset, tests, reproduction, API, and web demo run without
an API key, GPU, private data, external database, or live internet.

## Reproduce the deterministic pipeline

```bash
make reproduce-mini
```

That single command:

1. regenerates 16 synthetic cases and split metadata;
2. collects factual episodes into SQLite;
3. validates hash chains and rebuilds memory views;
4. runs exact paired removals for every active record under both estimands;
5. computes placebo controls, pairwise interactions, and Monte Carlo Shapley;
6. trains a CPU ridge outcome-model approximation;
7. calibrates uncertainty on the calibration split;
8. applies the conservative fixed-budget policy;
9. evaluates development, test, and shifted-test episodes at matched budgets;
10. generates JSON, CSV, SVG, LaTeX, Markdown, and a content-hashed manifest.

Primary outputs:

```text
artifacts/mini/
├── ledger.sqlite3
├── exact-effects.csv
├── effects.json
├── effect-model.json
├── effect-predictions.json
├── policy-decisions.json
├── evaluation.json
├── figures/
│   ├── effect-prediction.svg
│   └── matched-budget-success.svg
├── report.md
└── reproducibility-manifest.json
```

Generated artifacts are intentionally ignored by Git.

## Verified smoke outcome

The current deterministic run executes:

- 16 factual episodes across five splits;
- 32 total-system and 32 controlled-direct exact record effects;
- three paired seeds per exact effect;
- four pairwise interaction diagnostics;
- 32-sample Shapley on the known synergy coalition;
- 16 placebo negative controls;
- 32 Python tests and one React flow test.

Latest held-out smoke metrics are generated from executed artifacts, not entered by hand:

| Metric | Result |
|---|---:|
| Learned policy success | 0.625 |
| Strongest non-oracle fixed baseline | 0.625 |
| Paired policy improvement | 0.000 |
| Effect MAE | 0.649 |
| Effect Spearman | 0.234 |
| Effect sign accuracy | 0.364 |
| Placebo false-positive rate | 0.000 |

Interpretation: the replay and attribution machinery is functional, but the tiny linear effect model
does not establish the central scientific thesis. `evaluation.json` keeps the publication kill
criteria visible and unmet; [limitations](reports/limitations.md) defines the negative-result analysis.
The [completion report](reports/completion-report.md) records actual command outcomes, integrity
checks, environment-dependent skips, and the strongest defensible claim.

## Command reference

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `make setup` | Create the virtual environment and install locked Python/web dependencies |
| `make lint` | Ruff and ESLint |
| `make typecheck` | Strict mypy and TypeScript checks |
| `make test` | Python unit/integration/security/failure tests and Vitest |
| `make mini-data` | Generate MiniMemIntervene |
| `make collect-mini` | Collect factual episodes and memory events |
| `make intervene-mini` | Run exact effects, placebos, interactions, and Shapley |
| `make train-effect-mini` | Train and calibrate the effect predictor |
| `make train-policy-mini` | Produce conservative memory policy decisions |
| `make eval-mini` | Evaluate attribution and end-to-end outcomes |
| `make paper-smoke` | Generate the LaTeX table from executed metrics and validate sections |
| `make reproduce-mini` | Run the complete deterministic research pipeline |
| `make web-build` | Build the production React bundle |
| `make demo` | Serve the API and built UI on localhost |
| `make docker-up` | Build and run the constrained container |
| `make docker-test` | Execute the Python test stage in Docker |

On Windows, replace `make` with `.\make.cmd`.

## Scientific contracts

### Record necessity

For removal, the exact effect is:

```text
effect = Y(full memory, seed) - Y(memory without target, same seed)
```

Positive means useful or necessary influence; negative means harmful influence under the registered
protocol.

### Two estimands

- **Controlled-direct:** factual retrieval identities and token budget remain fixed; only memory
  visibility or representation changes.
- **Total-system:** retrieval, context assembly, action selection, and environment outcome are
  recomputed. This is the primary policy target.

### Four replay modes

- full deterministic environment replay;
- suffix replay with recorded tool results and off-manifold detection;
- one-step decision replay, explicitly local;
- non-generative scoring proxy, explicitly approximate.

All cache keys include checkpoint, intervention, policy/model revision, retriever/index, environment
snapshot, decoding/replay configuration, and seed.

### Estimators

- exact paired leave-one-out;
- representation and link interventions;
- matched-distractor validation;
- pairwise interaction;
- Monte Carlo Shapley with interval estimates;
- ridge outcome-model approximation with calibration;
- doubly robust ATE only when propensities, overlap, aligned arrays, and cross-fitting pass. Otherwise
  the API raises an assumption error and does not use a causal label.

### Model providers

The offline path uses the revisioned `rule-agent` and includes a deterministic test provider. Optional
adapters support a caller-initialized local Hugging Face generator, an explicitly allowlisted
OpenAI-compatible endpoint, and vLLM's compatible endpoint. External providers require pinned model
revisions, validate structured decisions against the registered action set, treat stored memory as
untrusted data, and convert timeouts, outages, or malformed output into typed replay failures. The
default setup never downloads model weights or makes a network request. See
[provider contracts](docs/providers.md).

## MiniMemIntervene

The bundled CC0 benchmark includes unique necessity, redundancy, synergy, stale memory, semantic
distractors, stored prompt injection, summary loss, summary denoising, raw restoration, useful and
misleading links, superseded preference, fixed-budget competition, rank displacement, paired
stochastic outcomes, off-manifold replay, unavailable/timeout providers, privacy denial, and
complete-memory failure primitives.

The rule agent chooses from observable evidence weights, retrieval, active links, and registered
synergies. The environment alone holds `correct_action`. Templates and entity pools are split across
train/calibration/development/test/shifted-test.

Public adapters are implemented for MemoryArena, MemoryAgentBench, LoCoMo, LongMemEval, and optional
LongMemEval-V2. They validate typed local manifests, required domain or competency coverage, path
containment, file sizes, and SHA-256 hashes before loading normalized official JSONL. Official data is
not bundled; absent data produces a clear skipped state and never silently substitutes
MiniMemIntervene. See the [public dataset contract](docs/public-datasets.md).

## API

The local service provides typed, paginated endpoints for:

- episode discovery and immutable ledger reads;
- memory reconstruction at logical time;
- retrieval;
- intervention replay with idempotency;
