- exact total/direct effects;
- predicted-effect-backed policy decisions;
- benchmark reproduction;
- JSONL trace export and reproducibility manifest download.

OpenAPI is available at `/api/openapi.json`. The React console uses the same endpoints; its replay
result is computed from reconstructed ledger state, not canned frontend data.

## Interface

The web application includes an episode browser, event timeline, time-versioned memory table, lineage
DAG, status views, exact effect comparison, intervention builder, factual/counterfactual action diff,
estimand labels, storage-budget slider, policy operations, trace export, and reproducibility metadata.
It displays observable actions, memory, tool/event metadata, and reason codes—never hidden
chain-of-thought.

## Security and privacy

Implemented controls include parameterized SQL, append-only triggers, owner/access fields, restricted
memory exclusion, secret/PII redaction hooks, prompt-injection flags, path validation, egress
allowlisting, request size/rate limits, defensive response headers, idempotency, container capability
drop, and a loopback default.

The local `X-Actor-ID` header is an integration hook, not production authentication. Before deployment,
add verified identity, row-level authorization, TLS, encryption, secrets management, user-facing
physical deletion, retention policy, backups, monitoring, and an audited egress proxy. Read the
[threat model](docs/threat-model.md) and [security policy](SECURITY.md).

## Repository layout

```text
memintervene/
├── apps/web/                 # React + TypeScript replay console
├── src/memintervene/         # Ledger, memory, replay, estimators, policy, API
├── data/mini_memintervene/   # Generated synthetic benchmark
├── configs/                  # Smoke and optional research configurations
├── tests/                    # Unit, integration, security, failure injection
├── docs/                     # Architecture, protocol, ADRs, threat model
├── paper/                    # LaTeX skeleton and generated-table hook
├── reports/                  # Data, model, ethics, limitations, scope
├── scripts/                  # Windows task and reproduction runners
├── Dockerfile
├── compose.yaml
├── Makefile
└── pyproject.toml
```

## Citation and license

Apache-2.0. Citation metadata is in [CITATION.cff](CITATION.cff).

documents.title: memintervene — docs/architecture.md
documents.content:
# Architecture

MemIntervene separates immutable observations from derived memory state and replayed outcomes.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    O[Observation and action events] --> L[(Append-only SQLite ledger)]
    L --> M[Deterministic materializer]
    M --> V[Versioned memory view]
    V --> R[Retriever and rule agent]
    V --> I[Typed intervention]
    I --> B[Counterfactual branch]
    B --> R2[Recomputed retrieval and action]
    R --> E[Paired effect]
    R2 --> E
    E --> P[Effect predictor]
    P --> C[Conservative fixed-budget policy]
```

## Boundaries

- `ledger.py` owns persistence, hash chaining, idempotency, and append-only database triggers.
- `memory.py` reconstructs records and links from events; it does not query outcome labels.
- `interventions.py` applies reversible state transformations without deleting immutable source events.
- `replay.py` owns replay modes, validity statuses, paired seeds, cache keys, and exact effects.
- `estimators.py` owns Shapley, guarded doubly robust estimation, the smoke effect model, and metrics.
- `policy.py` consumes predicted utility under storage, risk, and uncertainty penalties.
- `benchmark.py` defines the MiniMemIntervene environment. The rule agent only observes memory votes;
  the correct action is held by the environment scorer.
- `api.py` exposes typed local endpoints and serves the built React application.

## State model

The event ledger is the source of truth. A materialized record has stable identity, monotonically
increasing version, content hash, immutable source-event IDs, parent lineage, bitemporal boundaries,
status, privacy label, operation history, and index metadata. `FORGET` and `QUARANTINE` change the
active view; they never erase the ledger.

## Data stores

SQLite is the default transactional ledger. JSON, JSONL, CSV, SVG, and Markdown are used for compact
offline artifacts. The event interface keeps model output references hash-addressable so a production
adapter can move large traces to Parquet or object storage without changing replay semantics.

documents.title: memintervene — docs/adr/0001-offline-first.md
documents.content:
# ADR 0001: Offline-first deterministic reference path

Status: accepted

The default dataset, model, retriever, environment, tests, replay, API, and web demo must run without
an API key, private data, GPU, external database, or network after dependencies are installed.

This makes scientific and engineering failures reproducible. Open-weight and public-benchmark adapters
remain optional research configurations and must report unavailable prerequisites explicitly.

documents.title: memintervene — docs/adr/0002-append-only-ledger.md
documents.content:
# ADR 0002: Append-only ledger with rebuildable views

Status: accepted

Memory lifecycle operations are events, not destructive row mutations. SQLite triggers reject update
and delete operations, each branch is hash-chained, and materialized views are reconstructed in logical
time order.

This preserves provenance and enables replay, but it is only appropriate for synthetic/public research
traces. Production user deletion requires a separate physical-deletion and key-destruction design.

documents.title: memintervene — docs/providers.md
documents.content:
# Model providers

The deterministic `rule-agent` is the default provider and is the only provider executed by the smoke
pipeline and CI. It uses observable memory features and never receives the benchmark answer label.

Optional provider adapters:

- `LocalHuggingFaceProvider` wraps a caller-initialized local generation function. The caller owns
  loading, device placement, and optional quantization; MemIntervene requires a frozen model revision.
- `OpenAICompatibleProvider` calls a chat-completions-compatible endpoint only when its hostname is in
  an explicit allowlist.
- `VLLMProvider` uses the same protocol with a distinct provider identity for experiment manifests.

All adapters build prompts from the task, allowed actions, and retrieved records only. Stored memory
is labeled as untrusted data. Responses must be JSON and must select a registered candidate action;
scores, confidence, and reason codes are schema-checked. Timeouts, endpoint failures, and malformed
outputs become typed replay statuses instead of silent fallbacks or scored task outcomes.

The default setup does not install model frameworks, download weights, read an API key, or make a
network request. External credentials are passed explicitly by deployment code and must not be stored
in repository configuration.

documents.title: memintervene — docs/public-datasets.md
documents.content:
# Public dataset adapters

MemIntervene never downloads or redistributes public benchmark data in the default path. Each adapter
expects an official, locally normalized JSONL export under:

```text
data/public/<dataset_slug>/
├── manifest.json
└── records.jsonl
```

Supported adapters are `MemoryArena`, `MemoryAgentBench`, `LoCoMo`, `LongMemEval`, and optional
`LongMemEval-V2`. MemoryArena accepts `recorded`, `offline_snapshot`, or explicitly enabled `live`
manifests; the remaining adapters accept `official_files`.

The manifest is strict and rejects unknown fields:

```json
{
  "dataset": "MemoryArena",
  "version": "<official immutable revision>",
  "source": "<official source URL>",
  "license": "<upstream license>",
  "redistribution_status": "local official files only",
  "preprocessing_script": "scripts/normalize_memoryarena.py",
  "split_provenance": "official untouched test split",
  "privacy_handling": "no private user memory",
  "annotation_provenance": "official annotations",
  "mode": "recorded",
  "coverage": [
    "web_shopping",
    "group_travel",
    "progressive_web_search",
    "mathematics",
    "physics"
  ],
  "files": [
    {
      "path": "records.jsonl",
      "sha256": "<lowercase SHA-256>",
      "bytes": 12345,
      "split": "test"
    }
  ]
}
```

Validation checks dataset identity, mode, required coverage, path containment, file size, SHA-256,
JSONL syntax, and object-shaped records. Loading adds an `_adapter` envelope with dataset, version,
split, and mode. The adapter intentionally does not reinterpret upstream licenses or silently
substitute MiniMemIntervene.

documents.title: certicompress — README.md
documents.content:
# CertiCompress

CertiCompress is a working research and engineering system for proof-carrying memory consolidation in action-coupled agents.

Long-running agents collect more history than they can serve efficiently. A short summary can save tokens, but a fluent summary is not enough when memory changes tool calls, safety decisions, schedules, budgets, or user preferences. CertiCompress treats every consolidation as an untrusted proposal. A proposal becomes active only after it passes typed semantic checks, provenance checks, and deterministic behavior replay.

The project runs fully offline. It includes an append-only event ledger, deletable encrypted payloads, lineage tracking, nine consolidation operators, three replay levels, certificate lifecycle management, rate-distortion optimization, a FastAPI service, a React research console, tests, Docker support, generated reports, and a reproducible technical paper.

## What the system guarantees

For the included deterministic fixtures, an active derived memory has:

- Exact source event and source span references
- Typed checks for negation, modality, dates, numbers, units, preferences, and control-text injection
- Controlled direct, bounded horizon, and total system replay evidence
- A versioned certificate bound to the candidate, probes, dependencies, and verifier outputs
- Automatic raw-memory fallback when evidence is missing or a dependency becomes stale

A certificate is evidence for a finite test distribution and a specific dependency manifest. It is not a universal proof that two language model systems behave identically in every environment.

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["Append-only event ledger"] --> B["Claims and exact source spans"]
    B --> C["Candidate operators"]
    C --> D["Typed and semantic checks"]
    C --> E["Three-level replay"]
    B --> F["Provenance verification"]
    D --> G["Certificate authority"]
    E --> G
    F --> G
    G --> H{"Certificate valid"}
    H -->|Yes| I["Active derived memory"]
    H -->|No| J["Raw fallback"]
    I --> K["Rate-distortion optimizer"]
    L["Dependency or source change"] --> M["Selective invalidation"]
    M --> J
```

The ledger stores immutable typed events and content hashes. Raw text lives in a separate encrypted payload store so an authorized deletion can remove content without rewriting the audit trail. The lineage graph connects events, spans, claims, candidates, probes, and certificates.

## Quick start

Requirements:

- Python 3.11 or newer
- Node.js 20 or newer
- npm 10 or newer

Linux and macOS:

```bash
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
make setup
make test
make reproduce-mini
```

Windows PowerShell:

```powershell
py -3.11 -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
.\make.cmd setup
.\make.cmd test
.\make.cmd reproduce-mini
```

Start the API and web console:

```bash
make demo
```

On Windows use:

```powershell
.\make.cmd demo
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:5173` for the console and `http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs` for the API.

## Run one verified episode

```bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/episodes \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: lunch-demo-1" \
  -d '{
    "case_id": "lunch-demo",
    "memory": [
      "Maya is allergic to peanuts.",
      "Meals must avoid peanut sauce."
    ],
    "query": "Choose a safe lunch",
    "required_terms": ["allergic", "peanut"],
    "safe_action": "order_safe_meal",
    "unsafe_action": "order_standard_meal",
    "safe_arguments": {"allergen": "peanut"}
  }'
```

The response identifies the episode, extracted claims, generated candidates, and the active certified candidate. Inspect the full evidence with `GET /v1/episodes/lunch-demo`.

## Reproducible mini benchmark

`make reproduce-mini` runs the tracked synthetic benchmark and regenerates the metrics, certificates, lineage export, Pareto frontier, LaTeX table, and technical report.

The current checked run produced:

| Metric | Result |
| --- | ---: |
| Cases | 8 |
| Candidates evaluated | 102 |
| Unsafe candidates detected | 43 |
| Raw active tokens | 149 |
| Selected active tokens | 60 |
| Compression ratio | 0.403 |
| Selective invalidations | 6 |
| Re-certified candidates | 6 |

The zero empirical distortion in this run applies only to accepted candidates on the finite deterministic fixtures. Rejected candidates are not served.

Useful outputs:

- `reports/generated/metrics.json`
- `reports/generated/smoke-report.md`
- `reports/generated/rate-distortion-frontier.svg`
- `reports/generated/reproducibility-manifest.json`
- `paper/generated/certicompress-paper.pdf`

## Commands

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `make setup` | Install Python and web dependencies |
| `make lint` | Run Ruff and ESLint |
| `make typecheck` | Run mypy and the production web build |
| `make test` | Run Python and React tests |
| `make test-replay` | Run deterministic replay tests |
| `make test-streaming` | Run ledger streaming tests |
| `make smoke` | Run all mini fixtures and write evidence |
| `make benchmark-small` | Write the compact benchmark summary |
| `make paper-smoke` | Build the technical report from real metrics |
| `make reproduce-mini` | Regenerate all small reproducibility artifacts |
| `make demo` | Start the API and web console |
| `make docker-up` | Build and start the Docker services |
| `make docker-test` | Run Python tests in the API container |

Use `make.cmd` instead of `make` on a Windows machine without GNU Make.

## Consolidation operators

The candidate generator covers `RETAIN_RAW`, `EXTRACT`, `MERGE`, `ABSTRACT`, `REWRITE`, `SPLIT`, `LINK`, `QUARANTINE`, and `REJECT`.

Every operator emits the same typed candidate contract. Lossy candidates usually fail provenance or behavioral checks unless their retained evidence is sufficient. The engine activates the smallest eligible candidate for each case. The global optimizer then computes a certified frontier under a serving budget and risk target.

## Certificate lifecycle

Certificates move through explicit states:

`PROPOSED -> CHECKING -> CERTIFIED -> ACTIVE`

Source changes, payload deletion, model changes, prompt changes, retriever changes, tool schema changes, verifier changes, and environment changes can move a certificate to `STALE`. A stale certificate cannot remain active. Re-certification creates fresh evidence under the new dependency manifest.

The JSON contract is documented in `schemas/certificate.schema.json`.

## Dataset policy

`MiniCertiCompress` is an original synthetic fixture set released as CC0-1.0. It covers safety constraints, quantities, temporal order, preference supersession, group conflicts, tool arguments, and delayed behavioral effects.

Public dataset adapters are interfaces only. This repository does not redistribute third-party datasets. Users must download each dataset from its official source and comply with its license and terms.

## Originality and source boundaries

Private reference papers were used only to understand the broad research problem. They are not included in this repository. The project does not reproduce their text, figures, tables, screenshots, datasets, author names, institution names, or bibliography.

The implementation, architecture, names, diagrams, synthetic fixtures, experiments, documentation, and generated technical report were created independently for this project. CertiCompress does not claim authorship of, endorsement by, or affiliation with any external publication.

The full review boundary is recorded in `docs/originality-and-source-boundaries.md`.

## Repository map

```text
apps/api                 FastAPI entry point
apps/web                 React research console
data/mini_certicompress  Original synthetic fixtures
docs                     Architecture, protocols, and decisions
migrations               Alembic event projection migration
paper                    Reproducible technical report
reports                  Model, data, ethics, and run reports
schemas                  Public JSON contracts
scripts                  Cross-platform task and reproduction commands
src/certicompress        Core Python package
tests                    Unit, integration, replay, API, and streaming tests
```

## Security model

Memory is always treated as data, never as executable control text. The validator identifies common instruction-injection patterns and rejects unsafe candidates. Tenant IDs scope ledger reads and writes. Request sizes are bounded. Mutating API routes require idempotency keys. Raw payload content is encrypted at rest and can be cryptographically erased.

This is a research implementation, not a hardened secrets manager. Review `SECURITY.md` and `docs/threat-model.md` before using it with sensitive or regulated data.

## Development

The default workflow is:

```bash
make lint
make typecheck
make test
make smoke
```

CI repeats these checks on Python 3.11 and Node.js 20. Docker is optional for local development.

## Project status

Version 0.1.0 is an end-to-end reference implementation. The deterministic local policy and semantic adapter make the evidence inspectable and keep the test suite offline. Production deployments should replace those adapters with calibrated models, stronger sandboxing, signed certificates, durable key management, and task-specific replay environments.

## License

The code is available under the Apache License 2.0. The synthetic fixture dataset is available under CC0-1.0.

documents.title: certicompress — docs/architecture.md
documents.content:
# Architecture

CertiCompress separates the write path, evidence path, and serving path.

## Write path

The SQLite ledger accepts typed events through an append-only API. Each record binds parent events, logical time, schema version, model dependencies, and a content hash. Raw text is written to an encrypted payload store and referenced by ID. Deleting a payload does not rewrite the ledger.

The optional SQLAlchemy projection and Alembic migration provide a conventional integration point for larger services.

## Evidence path

Deterministic extraction emits exact source spans and typed claims. The lineage graph records every derivation. Candidate generation applies all nine operators through one typed contract.

Verification has four layers:

1. Typed preservation checks
2. Deterministic semantic stance checks
3. Exact provenance and ancestry checks
4. Paired behavior replay

The certificate authority combines these results with dependency versions and risk bounds. The integrity hash covers the complete certificate body.

## Serving path

Only a candidate with a valid certificate can become active. The per-case selector prefers the smallest eligible candidate. The global optimizer chooses at most one candidate per case under an active-rate budget and distortion bound.

Invalidation is dependency-aware. A source event or version change marks only affected certificates stale. The serving path falls back to raw memory until a fresh certificate becomes active.

## Storage choices

SQLite keeps the reference implementation easy to run and audit. The store interfaces are narrow enough to replace with PostgreSQL or an event streaming backend. The lineage graph is in memory for the demo and exported as JSON after benchmark runs.

documents.title: certicompress — docs/adr/0001-append-only-ledger.md
documents.content:
# ADR 0001: Append-only ledger with separate payload deletion

## Status

Accepted

## Decision

Typed audit events are immutable after append. Raw text is stored in a separate encrypted payload database and referenced by opaque ID.

## Consequences

Event integrity can be checked without retaining deleted content. A payload deletion invalidates dependent certificates and leaves a non-sensitive audit record. Operators must back up and rotate the two stores according to different policies.

documents.title: certicompress — docs/adr/0002-fail-closed-activation.md
documents.content:
# ADR 0002: Fail-closed activation

## Status

Accepted

## Decision

Only candidates with a valid certificate can enter active serving state. Missing evidence, failed checks, stale dependencies, and integrity errors select raw fallback.

## Consequences

Compression availability can decrease during incidents or upgrades, but unverified derived memory is never served as trusted state.

documents.title: certicompress — docs/originality-and-source-boundaries.md
documents.content:
# Originality and source boundaries

## Purpose

This note records how CertiCompress was separated from private reference material during development. It exists to make the project history clear and to avoid presenting another person's publication as part of this work.

## How reference material was used

Private papers were reviewed only for broad problem orientation. The useful high-level questions were:

- How can agent memory stay structured as it changes over time
- How can a system preserve temporal and semantic relationships
- How can memory updates be evaluated instead of accepted on fluency alone
- How should an agent fall back when a derived memory is not trustworthy

These questions are general research topics. The implementation choices in this repository were developed independently around proof-carrying consolidation, deterministic replay, typed constraints, certificate lifecycle management, and rate-distortion selection.

## Material intentionally excluded

The repository does not contain:

- The private reference PDF files
- Extracted pages, screenshots, figures, or tables from those files
- Copied or lightly rewritten passages
- Names of the papers, authors, institutions, or publication venues
- Bibliographic entries for the private papers
- Code, datasets, prompts, or experimental results taken from those papers
- Claims that the external publications belong to this project

## Material created for CertiCompress

The following assets were created specifically for this repository:

- Python implementation and public interfaces
- FastAPI service and React research console
- Ledger, lineage, payload deletion, replay, certificate, and optimizer design
- MiniCertiCompress synthetic fixtures and evaluation partitions
- Tests, migrations, Docker setup, CI workflow, and command runner
- Architecture diagrams, documentation, model card, data statement, and threat model
- Benchmark results generated by executing the local implementation
- Self-contained technical report generated from those executed results

The synthetic records use fictional scenarios and do not copy examples from private papers or external datasets.

## Attribution position

CertiCompress makes no claim of authorship, ownership, endorsement, or affiliation regarding any external publication. The repository name, code, dataset, report, and documentation identify only this independent implementation.

This record improves transparency but is not legal advice and cannot guarantee that no third party will ever raise a claim. Anyone preparing a commercial release should perform an independent license and intellectual property review.

## Verification checklist

Before each release:

1. Search tracked files for private paper filenames and identifying names
2. Confirm that no source PDF is tracked
3. Confirm that generated benchmark values come from the repository code
4. Confirm that synthetic data remains original
5. Review new assets for copied text, figures, tables, or screenshots
6. Keep external datasets outside the repository

documents.title: certicompress — docs/public-datasets.md
documents.content:
# Public dataset adapters

The package contains adapter interfaces for external evaluation data. It does not download or redistribute third-party datasets.

Each adapter should:

1. Validate the expected local file layout
2. Convert records to the common episode schema
3. Record source version and license metadata
4. Preserve the original train and test boundary
5. Keep calibration data separate from final evaluation data

Users are responsible for obtaining data from its official source and following the relevant license, access rules, and usage restrictions.

documents.title: tempo-trust — README.md
documents.content:
# TEMPO-Trust

Claim-conditioned online source reliability for evidence systems that operate under drift, copying, and delayed feedback.

TEMPO-Trust answers a practical question: what should an evidence agent do when a source that has been reliable in general becomes unreliable for one topic?

The system keeps trust local to source, topic, claim type, time, and detected regime. It converts documents into atomic claims, scores evidence stance, groups dependent sources before aggregation, detects abrupt reliability changes, and abstains when independent support is too weak. Every state transition and answer decision is recorded in a checksummed provenance ledger.

This repository includes the research core, a deterministic streaming benchmark, a FastAPI service, a React dashboard, evaluation and calibration utilities, dataset adapters, paper asset generation, tests, containers, and CI.

## Why this project exists

A single reputation score is too coarse for a changing evidence environment.

A source may remain accurate on climate policy while failing on medicine. Several sites may repeat the same upstream report and appear to provide independent confirmation. Audits may arrive late or never arrive. A safe system must update online without using future labels, distinguish copying from corroboration, detect meaningful changes, and expose the evidence behind every decision.

TEMPO-Trust is designed around those requirements.

## System behavior

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Typed source and document events] --> B[Atomic claims]
    B --> C[Probabilistic stance]
    C --> D[Provenance and dependence graph]
    D --> E[Hierarchical trust posterior]
    E --> F[Online change detection]
    F --> G[Policy decision]
    G --> H[Answer, retrieve, audit, explain, or abstain]
    A --> L[(Append-only ledger)]
    B --> L
    C --> L
    D --> L
    E --> L
    F --> L
    G --> L
```

The default path is deterministic, offline, and CPU-only. It does not download a model or call an external service. The built-in claim extractor and stance scorer are transparent research fixtures, not substitutes for a production NLI model.

## Core design

### Claim-conditioned trust

Trust is represented as a source confusion model over support, refute, insufficient evidence, and malformed evidence. The posterior uses partial pooling across:

- Global behavior
- Source
- Topic
- Claim type
- Source and topic
- Source and claim type
- Source, topic, claim type, and current regime

Sparse scopes borrow strength from broader levels. Well-observed scopes become increasingly local.

### Online change detection

Audited outcomes are processed by a Bayesian online change-point detector. Persistence and cooldown rules reduce noisy alarms. A detected compromise opens a new reliability regime for the affected scope. Recovery is tracked separately.

### Dependence correction

Evidence is clustered using canonical URLs, content fingerprints, citation links, declared upstream sources, and token similarity. Fusion occurs at the cluster level before source reliability is applied. This prevents copied reports from being counted as independent corroboration.

### Decision policy

The policy uses posterior confidence, conflict mass, effective independent support, uncertainty, and an audit budget. It can:

- Answer
- Retrieve more independent evidence
- Request an audit
- Explain a conflict
- Abstain

The conservative default favors abstention over unsupported acceptance.

### Provenance ledger

The SQLite ledger is append-only at the database layer. Each event contains the previous checksum, its own checksum, a schema version, a trace identifier, and a typed payload. Deterministic replay rebuilds materialized state and verifies the chain.

Sensitive payloads are stored separately so a retention policy can erase content without corrupting the scientific event history.

## Quick start

Requirements:

- Python 3.11 or newer
- Node.js 22
- pnpm 10 or newer

Install the backend, install the dashboard dependencies, and build the dashboard:

```bash
python scripts/tasks.py setup
```

Start the local application:

```bash
python scripts/tasks.py demo
```

Open:

- Dashboard: `http://127.0.0.1:8000`
- API documentation: `http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs`
- Health check: `http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/health`

The dashboard controls a frozen 64-event stream. Run it to watch a medicine-only compromise, delayed audits, copied evidence, a detected regime change, and recovery.

## Reproduce the controlled evaluation

Run the smoke experiment:

```bash
python scripts/tasks.py smoke
```

Run the longer local benchmark:

```bash
python scripts/tasks.py benchmark-small
```

Verify that two independent executions produce the same logical result hash:

```bash
python scripts/tasks.py reproduce-mini
```

Generate figures and tables from measured outputs:

```bash
python scripts/tasks.py paper-smoke
```

Outputs are written below `reports/generated`. Paper assets are written below `paper/generated`. Generated results are excluded from version control because they are rebuilt from the frozen stream and configuration.

## Measured smoke result

The table below comes from a fresh local run of the frozen 64-event stream with seed `1729`.

| Measure | Result |
|---|---:|
| Compromise detection tick | 22 |
| Compromise detection delay | 4 events |
| Recovery detection tick | 46 |
| Recovery time | 4 events |
| False alarms | 0 |
| Answer accuracy at accepted coverage | 100% |
| Answer coverage | 17.19% |
| Unsupported answer rate | 0% |
| Overall binary accuracy | 90.63% |
| Brier score | 0.0684 |
| ECE with 10 bins | 0.1522 |
| Raw documents per claim | 5.09 |
| Effective independent support | 2.55 |
| Prompt injection cases answered | 0 of 1 |

The paired reproduction result hash is:

```text
35750e228e00c53260d2f2cd8ef2596c461a7cabdcb974e0912773af0cb8b04a
```

These measurements establish deterministic behavior on the included controlled stream. They do not establish real-world superiority. Answer accuracy is reported at selective coverage and should not be compared directly with full-coverage baselines.

## Evaluation protocol

The runner is strictly prequential:

1. Predict from the state available at the current tick
2. Record the decision and its provenance
3. Deliver only audits whose delay has elapsed
4. Update trust and change-point state
5. Continue to the next event

The stream contains stable periods, a topic-local abrupt compromise, a recovery period, dependent copies, lightweight sybil sources, missing labels, delayed audits, and one prompt injection fixture.

Reported metrics include:

- Selective answer accuracy and coverage
- False accept and unsupported answer rates
- Area under the risk-coverage curve
- Brier score, expected calibration error, and log loss
- Trust estimation error
- Compromise delay, recovery time, and false alarms
- Raw and effective support
- Retrieval, stance, audit, and ledger costs

Baselines include equal source voting, provenance-cluster voting, static global trust, static topic trust, recency weighting, and sliding-window reliability.

## Dataset adapters

The repository provides local JSONL adapters for:

- Claim verification records
- Multi-hop question answering records
- Timestamped CommunityFact-compatible records

Adapters validate manifests, timestamps, source identity fields, and future-evidence leakage. Datasets are not redistributed. A dataset manifest must record version, license, temporal cutoff policy, preprocessing version, source identity policy, and redistribution status.

## API overview

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/v1/health` | Readiness and ledger status |
| `POST` | `/v1/sources` | Register a typed source |
| `POST` | `/v1/documents` | Ingest a document and extract claims |
| `POST` | `/v1/claims/extract` | Extract atomic claims |
| `POST` | `/v1/stance/score` | Score support, refute, and insufficiency |
| `GET` | `/v1/trust/{source_id}` | Read scoped trust |
| `GET` | `/v1/trust/{source_id}/timeline` | Read trust history |
| `GET` | `/v1/provenance` | Read evidence lineage |
| `POST` | `/v1/decisions` | Fuse evidence and select an action |
| `POST` | `/v1/audits` | Submit delayed ground truth |
| `GET` | `/v1/alarms` | Read compromise and recovery alarms |
| `POST` | `/v1/replay` | Verify and replay the ledger |
| `GET` | `/v1/trace` | Read paginated event history |
| `POST` | `/v1/benchmark` | Run an isolated controlled benchmark |

Audit submission requires the header `X-Audit-Role: auditor`. Set `TEMPO_TRUST_API_KEY` to require an API key on all routes outside a trusted local environment.

## Quality checks

Run the same checks as CI:

```bash
python scripts/tasks.py lint
python scripts/tasks.py typecheck
python scripts/tasks.py test
python scripts/tasks.py test-streaming
```

The current suite contains 40 Python tests and one dashboard test. It covers the ledger, trust updates, change detection, provenance grouping, policy decisions, temporal diagnostics, API behavior, dataset leakage checks, security boundaries, privacy retention, calibration, statistics, and the full streaming scenario.

If Make is available, the same commands are exposed as `make lint`, `make typecheck`, `make test`, and `make test-streaming`.

## Docker

Build and run the application:

```bash
docker compose up --build
```

Run the test image:

```bash
docker compose --profile test run --rm tests
```

The runtime image uses an unprivileged user, a read-only root filesystem, a dedicated data volume, a health check, and `no-new-privileges`.

## Repository map

```text
apps/api                 ASGI entry point
apps/web                 React and TypeScript dashboard
configs                  Frozen runtime configuration
data/mini_tempo_trust    Controlled stream manifest
paper                    Manuscript support and generated asset pipeline
reports                  Experiment output contract
scripts                  Cross-platform task runner
src/tempo_trust          Research and service implementation
tests                    Unit, API, security, and streaming tests
```

The main implementation modules are:

- `claims` for atomic claim extraction
- `stance` for probabilistic evidence labels
- `sources` for source identity and conservative merges
- `provenance` for dependence and lineage
- `trust` for hierarchical online posteriors
- `changepoint` for compromise and recovery detection
- `aggregation` for cluster-first evidence fusion
- `policy` for answer and abstention decisions
- `ledger` for checksummed event history and replay
- `evaluation` for metrics, baselines, calibration, bias checks, and statistics

## Security and privacy

The service validates URL schemes, blocks private and non-routable addresses by default, rejects embedded credentials, enforces MIME and payload limits, sanitizes rendered text, redacts common secret formats, rate limits clients, and applies restrictive response headers.

Prompt-like instructions found inside retrieved content are treated as untrusted evidence. They are labeled and logged but never executed.

See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) for the threat model and reporting process.

## Scope and limitations

This is a research-grade reference implementation with a complete local execution path. It is not a truth oracle and it is not ready for unsupervised use in high-stakes decisions.

Important limitations:

- The default stance scorer is deterministic and lexical
- Real deployments need a calibrated domain model and monitored model versions
- Source identity and provenance errors can distort independence estimates
- Missing audits can create selection bias
- Genuine truth changes can resemble source compromise
- Synthetic evaluation does not prove external validity
- The current persistence layer targets one local process

The kill criterion is explicit: a candidate trust method should adapt faster than static and recency-based systems during compromise without harming stable-period performance. External claims should be made only after paired, leakage-controlled evaluation on licensed data.

## Research artifacts

The `paper` directory contains a compact manuscript scaffold, data statement, model card, ethics and limitations note, licensing table, and reproducibility checklist. Figures, tables, and metric macros are generated from an executed run. Hand-entered result tables are not part of the workflow.

## License

Apache License 2.0. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).

documents.title: tempo-trust — ARCHITECTURE.md
documents.content:
# Architecture

TEMPO-Trust separates evidence processing, online learning, decision policy, and auditability. Each stage accepts typed records and emits a ledger event.

## Processing path

1. Register sources with conservative identity rules
2. Ingest a typed document
3. Extract atomic claims with topic, claim type, and valid time
4. Score each evidence and claim pair
5. Update provenance and dependence clusters
6. Fuse evidence once per independent cluster
7. Read the hierarchical reliability posterior
8. Select an answer, retrieval, audit, explanation, or abstention action
9. Record the complete decision trace
10. Apply delayed audits when they become available
11. Update trust and online change detection

The prediction always precedes its audit. This ordering prevents label leakage in streaming evaluation.

## State boundaries

The engine owns:

- Source registry
- Document and claim records
- Evidence records
- Provenance graph
- Hierarchical trust state
- Change-point detectors
- Policy budget
- Alarm history
- Trust timeline

The ledger remains the authoritative event history. Materialized state can be rebuilt and checked against the live state hash.

## Trust update

Each audited evidence item contributes fractional sufficient statistics using its stance probability vector. Recent observations receive more weight through exponential decay. The full source, topic, claim type, and regime posterior is partially pooled with broader scopes.

The model intentionally separates:

- Source quality from source identity
- Relevance from correctness
- Independent support from repeated support
- Gradual decay from abrupt regime change
- Source compromise from possible truth change

## Extension points

Production integrations can replace:

- `claims/extractor.py` with a structured claim model
- `stance/scorer.py` with a calibrated NLI service
- `provenance/graph.py` with a richer citation graph
- `datasets/adapters.py` with licensed benchmark loaders
- SQLite with a transactional event store

Keep schema versions, model versions, configuration hashes, and replay tests when replacing a component.

documents.title: temporags — README.md
documents.content:
# TempoRGS

Reader-aware parallel anytime reranker-guided graph search under latency budgets

[![CI](https://github.com/pxnkit/temporags/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/pxnkit/temporags/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-244c46)](LICENSE)
[![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.11%2B-244c46)](pyproject.toml)

TempoRGS is an executable research system for studying how a document graph can use several complementary frontier regions at once, rerank them in parallel, and return the best valid ranking before a deadline.

The repository contains an original implementation, original fixture data, and measurements generated by its own commands.

## What runs today

The default profile runs offline on CPU after dependency installation. It uses a deterministic MiniTempoRGS corpus and does not require an API key, GPU, model download, vector database, or external benchmark.

It includes:

- BM25-style sparse retrieval and deterministic hashing-based dense retrieval
- Weighted hybrid seed selection
- A versioned exact kNN document graph with corpus and embedding hashes
- A strict frontier state machine
- A faithful sequential greedy RGS baseline for the pointwise scoring setting
- Within-query parallel batch selection
- Random, top-B, cluster round-robin, MMR, DPP-style, submodular, UCB, and learned-score policies
- A bounded asynchronous reranker pool with microbatching, deadlines, cancellation outcomes, and scheduler metrics
- Globally comparable pointwise scores with model provenance
- CPU gain and latency models with calibrated residual intervals
- Deadline-aware and reader-aware stopping
- Separate retrieval ranking and reader context selection
- FastAPI endpoints and a React research console
- Unit, integration, concurrency, deadline, failure, API, and security tests
- Docker, CI, reproducibility manifests, and paper assets

The exact implementation boundary is documented in [reports/COMPLETION.md](reports/COMPLETION.md).

## Validated result

The local validation run passed 29 Python tests, Ruff, Python compilation, TypeScript checking, the Vite production build, live API requests, and the browser query-to-trace flow.

On the four-query deterministic smoke fixture, TempoRGS returned mean nDCG@10 of 0.7929 in 65.97 ms. Sequential RGS returned 0.7896 in 69.22 ms. These are engineering smoke measurements, not benchmark or publication results.

The small policy benchmark did not support the diversity hypothesis. Top-B was stronger than MMR and submodular batching on mean nDCG@10 and p95 latency in this fixture.

See [reports/VALIDATION.md](reports/VALIDATION.md) for the exact command outcomes, interruption result, policy table, environment, and claim boundary.

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Q["Query and deadline"] --> S["Sparse and dense seeds"]
    S --> G["Versioned document graph"]
    G --> F["Typed frontier"]
    F --> P["Diversity-aware batch policy"]
    P --> A["Async reranker pool"]
    A --> R["Valid global ranking"]
    R --> C{"Continue or stop"}
    C -->|continue| G
    C -->|stop| X["Reader-aware context"]
    R --> T["Versioned anytime trace"]
```

Every synchronization boundary contains a deterministic top-k ranking that depends only on completed scores. Unfinished jobs are never required to interpret the current ranking.

## Quick start

### Python service and research pipeline

```bash
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -e ".[dev]"
pytest -q
python scripts/run_smoke.py
python scripts/run_demo.py
```

On PowerShell, activate the environment with:

```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
```

The API is available at `http://127.0.0.1:8000` and the OpenAPI page is available at `http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs`.

### Web console

```bash
cd apps/web
pnpm install
pnpm dev
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:5173`.

### Make targets

```bash
make setup
make lint
make typecheck
make test
make test-concurrency
make smoke
make benchmark-small
make paper-smoke
make demo
make docker-up
make docker-test
make reproduce-mini
```

`make smoke` builds the mini corpus graph, creates sparse and dense seeds, runs sequential RGS, generates counterfactual outcomes, fits gain and latency models, calibrates intervals, runs parallel search, forces an anytime interruption, evaluates retrieval and reader utility, and writes a report plus reproducibility manifest.

## Example request

```bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/search \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "query": "Which two controls reduce database tail latency during sudden traffic bursts",
    "policy": "submodular",
    "deadline_ms": 350,
    "batch_size": 3,
    "reader_profile": "noise_sensitive"
  }'
```

The response includes the final ranking, reader context, boundary events, selected and rejected actions, stop reason, score provenance, graph version, scheduler metrics, and reader metrics.

## Repository map

```text
apps/api                   FastAPI service
apps/web                   React and TypeScript research console
src/temporags/graphs       Graph protocol and exact kNN backend
src/temporags/retrievers   Sparse, dense, and hybrid seed retrieval
src/temporags/rerankers    Reranker protocol implementation
src/temporags/frontier     State machine and exactly-once accounting
src/temporags/scheduler    Async queue, batching, deadlines, and failures
src/temporags/policies     Parallel frontier policies
src/temporags/uncertainty  Gain and latency calibration
src/temporags/stopping     Anytime controller
src/temporags/readers      Reader profiles and context selection
src/temporags/datasets     Mini benchmark and local dataset adapters
src/temporags/evaluation   Retrieval and quality-time metrics
src/temporags/tracing      Versioned trace persistence
src/temporags/security     Input, path, and archive validation
data/mini_temporags        Redistributable deterministic fixture
tests                      Unit and integration suite
scripts                    Smoke, benchmark, demo, and paper commands
paper                      Paper skeleton and generated figures
reports                    Completion status and generated results
```

## Reproducibility

The smoke pipeline writes:

- `reports/smoke/smoke-report.json`
- `reports/smoke/reproducibility-manifest.json`
- `reports/smoke/counterfactual-outcomes.jsonl`
- `reports/smoke/mini-benchmark.csv`
- `reports/smoke/mini-graph.json`

The manifest records Python, platform, dependency versions, graph hashes, model revision, seed, executed stages, and stages that were not executed.

Run `python scripts/reproduce_mini.py` to create a separate reproduction directory.

## Dataset adapters

Local normalized JSONL adapters are included for BRIGHT, FollowIR, SciFact, and TREC Deep Learning. The repository does not download or redistribute those corpora.

Each corpus row must contain `doc_id`, `text`, and optional `title`, `cluster`, and `duplicate_group` fields.

Each query row must contain `query_id`, `text`, and a `relevant` mapping from document ID to relevance grade.

Adapters return a manifest with content hashes and source metadata.

## Citation

If TempoRGS supports your research, evaluation, or engineering work, cite the software using [CITATION.cff](CITATION.cff).

## Claim boundary

The deterministic scorer is a test fixture for search, scheduling, calibration, and serving behavior. It is not a substitute for a learned cross-encoder.

The repository does not claim results beyond the experiments recorded in its generated reports. Broader conclusions require public benchmark, open-model, transfer, and statistical protocols.

Generated reports contain only measurements produced by local commands.

## License

MIT License

documents.title: verifysplit — README.md
documents.content:
# VerifySplit

**Controlling shared failure in generator-verifier systems with independent
evidence.**

VerifySplit is offline-first research and engineering
workbench for a failure mode that ordinary self-verification misses: the
generator and verifier can agree because they inherit the same model,
trajectory, or evidence error.

The repository provides a complete deterministic vertical slice:

- a typed append-only SQLite event ledger.
- a branch, backtrack, prune, select, and replay trajectory DAG.
- evidence canonicalization, source clusters, mirrors, near duplicates, and
  provenance edges.
- same-family, independent answer-blind, evidence-only, and formal verification.
- calibrated false-accept risk intervals.
- a bounded one-step expected-value-of-information controller.
- MiniVerifySplit and MiniVerifyTool offline fixtures.
- FastAPI endpoints with server-sent event replay.
- a responsive React/TypeScript audit interface.
- CPU-only smoke, benchmark, paper, and reproducibility pipelines.

The default path uses no API key, GPU, proprietary model, live search service,
external database, or private benchmark.

## Status and claim boundary

This is a working research artifact and experiment harness, not evidence that
the full research thesis is already supported. The included smoke results are
generated from a synthetic deterministic fixture and must not be presented as
external-model or public-benchmark performance. External dataset and model
adapters are explicit opt-ins and never silently substitute for one another.

The strongest defensible claim from the default path is:

> VerifySplit can reproduce known shared-evidence failures, preserve a typed
> audit trace, detect provenance overlap, acquire a distinct source cluster,
> and select a risk-aware corrective action under a measured budget.

## Quick start

Prerequisites: Python 3.11+, Node.js 22+, npm, and GNU Make.

```bash
make setup
make test
make smoke
make demo
```

`make demo` starts:

- web workbench: `http://127.0.0.1:3010`
- API documentation: `http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs`

It also creates one real API run before reporting readiness.

For Windows PowerShell without Make:

```powershell
python -m pip install -e ".[dev]"
npm.cmd install
npm.cmd run build
python scripts\run_smoke.py
python scripts\demo.py
```

## Reproducible commands

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `make setup` | Install locked dependencies, build the web application, initialize local directories |
| `make lint` | Run Ruff and ESLint |
| `make typecheck` | Run mypy and TypeScript |
| `make test` | Run CPU-safe unit, integration, API, statistical, security, and failure tests |
| `make smoke` | Run the deterministic MiniVerifySplit vertical slice and generate reports |
| `make benchmark-small` | Produce an explicitly labeled local benchmark report |
| `make paper-smoke` | Validate paper sources and generated tables/figures |
| `make demo` | Launch the real FastAPI and React systems and execute a demo run |
| `make docker-up` | Build and start API and web containers |
| `make docker-test` | Test the API image |
| `make reproduce-mini` | Re-run from isolated state and compare deterministic hashes |

## Architecture

```text
question + budgets
        |
        v
relevant retrieval ----> canonical documents ----> source clusters
        |                                            |
        v                                            v
candidate trajectory                         shared-failure features
        |                                            |
        +---- shared verifier                         |
        +---- provenance-independent retrieval -------+
        +---- answer-blind verifier
        +---- deterministic formal checker
                         |
                         v
            one-step lower-bound utility
                         |
            answer / acquire / check / abstain
```

The Python research engine is in `src/verifysplit/`. The production browser
engine is in `lib/demo-engine.ts`. Both use the same public action set and
dependence-aware policy concepts. The browser path is self-contained so the
deployed workbench stays functional without an external Python host. The
FastAPI service is the authoritative local research API.

## Repository map

```text
apps/api/                 FastAPI entrypoint
apps/web/                 web deployment note
app/                      production React/Vinext interface
lib/                      deterministic browser engine
src/verifysplit/          research engine
data/mini_verifysplit/    redistributable offline benchmark
data/mini_verifytool/     deterministic action environment
configs/                  versioned providers, datasets, policies, experiments
tests/                    unit, integration, API, security, browser tests
scripts/                  smoke, benchmark, paper, demo, reproduction
paper/                    LaTeX skeleton and research statements
reports/                  generated-artifact documentation
docker/                   API and web container definitions
.github/workflows/        CPU-only continuous integration
```

## API

The versioned API implements:

```text
POST /api/v1/runs
GET  /api/v1/runs/{run_id}
POST /api/v1/runs/{run_id}/cancel
GET  /api/v1/runs/{run_id}/events
GET  /api/v1/runs/{run_id}/events/stream
GET  /api/v1/runs/{run_id}/trajectories
GET  /api/v1/runs/{run_id}/evidence
GET  /api/v1/runs/{run_id}/verifications
GET  /api/v1/runs/{run_id}/controller-decisions
POST /api/v1/interventions
POST /api/v1/evaluate
GET  /api/v1/experiments/{experiment_id}
GET  /api/v1/health
GET  /api/v1/providers
GET  /api/v1/datasets
```

IDs, limits, enums, URLs, paths, and payloads are validated. Failures use typed
HTTP responses. Retrieved text is untrusted data and never becomes a system
instruction.

## MiniVerifySplit

The fixture includes train, calibration, development, test, source shift,
corruption shift, tool shift, and failure-injection cases. It covers:

- same-model arithmetic and sign errors.
- mirrored and paraphrased upstream evidence.
- independent corroboration and refutation.
- stale facts, missing hops, and insufficient evidence.
- answer anchoring and answer-blind correction.
- formal pass, fail, and unsupported types.
- retriever/verifier timeout and malformed output.
- budget exhaustion and abstention.
- prompt injection and private-evidence denial.
- stale tool observations and action divergence.

Public datasets are adapters only until the user downloads and validates their
upstream files. The repository does not redistribute MATH-500, HotpotQA, or
MuSiQue.

## Security and privacy

- retrieved text is isolated from instructions.
- prompt injection is labeled.
- optional live retrieval blocks private, loopback, link-local, multicast, and
  credential-bearing URLs.
- local paths are root-scoped.
- SQL statements are parameterized.
- private evidence remains namespace-scoped.
- external private-evidence transmission is disabled by default.
- secrets are redacted from audit text.
- retries, rates, sizes, budgets, and interactions are bounded.
- visible traces contain summaries, evidence, measurements, tool activity, and
  reason codes, never hidden provider chain-of-thought.

See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md), [MODEL_CARD.md](MODEL_CARD.md), and
[DATA_STATEMENT.md](DATA_STATEMENT.md).

## License

Apache-2.0. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).

documents.title: verifysplit — docs/adr/0001-offline-first-vertical-slice.md
documents.content:
# ADR 0001: Offline-first deterministic vertical slice

Status: accepted

VerifySplit requires a default path that works without APIs, GPUs, live search,
external databases, or private benchmarks. The authoritative research engine is
therefore Python with SQLite, deterministic adapters, and synthetic fixtures.
Optional provider and public-dataset adapters fail clearly when unavailable.

The deployed browser workbench contains a TypeScript implementation of the same
public research concepts so it remains usable without a separately hosted Python
service. Its results are explicitly labeled fixture-only.

documents.title: verifysplit — docs/adr/0002-event-and-provenance-audit.md
documents.content:
# ADR 0002: Event and provenance audit

Status: accepted

Events are append-only, content-hashed, versioned, and keyed by run plus logical
time. SQLite is the default repository. Traces record concise project-authored
summaries, evidence, tool activity, measurements, and reason codes; they never
store hidden provider chain-of-thought.

Evidence independence is multi-level. Different URLs do not imply independence.
The controller reasons over canonical documents, source clusters, upstream
citations, near duplicates, organizations, snapshots, and measurement processes.

documents.title: evidroute — README.md
documents.content:
# EvidRoute

[![CI](https://github.com/pxnkit/evidroute/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/pxnkit/evidroute/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![Python 3.12](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-3.12-3776AB?logo=python&logoColor=white)](https://www.python.org/)
[![React 19](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-19-61DAFB?logo=react&logoColor=111827)](https://react.dev/)
[![MIT License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-22C55E.svg)](LICENSE)

EvidRoute is an offline-first research implementation of risk-constrained sequential evidence
routing. Given a query, resource budget, and risk target, the policy selects among heterogeneous
evidence sources or terminates with `ANSWER`, `ASK_USER`, or `ABSTAIN`.

The system provides typed route contracts, evidence normalization, citation tracking,
counterfactual route evaluation, selective-risk calibration, source-shift detection, and
replayable decision traces. The reference configuration is deterministic, CPU-compatible, and
does not require external credentials.

| Item | Status |
| --- | --- |
| Release | `0.1.0` research prototype |
| Reference evaluation | Synthetic MiniRoute benchmark |
| Public benchmark evaluation | Not yet executed |
| Default network policy | Offline |
| API | FastAPI |
| User interface | React and TypeScript |
| License | MIT |

## System model

At each decision step, the router observes the query, remaining budget, source health, prior
evidence, and configured risk target. It selects a feasible evidence route or a terminal action.
Each acquisition returns a normalized evidence bundle with provenance, cost, latency, and typed
failure information.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Q["Query, budget, risk target"] --> R["Routing policy"]
    R --> P["Parametric"]
    R --> M["Memory"]
    R --> S["Sparse or dense retrieval"]
    R --> G["Structured graph"]
    R --> W["Frozen web"]
    P --> E["Evidence normalization"]
    M --> E
    S --> E
    G --> E
    W --> E
    E --> C["Conflict, citation, and risk checks"]
    C --> A["ANSWER"]
    C --> U["ASK_USER"]
    C --> X["ABSTAIN"]
```

The decision loop is bounded by configurable limits on route calls, cost, latency, and retrieval
hops. A route is selected only when its estimated value exceeds its acquisition cost and the
resulting decision satisfies the applicable risk policy.

## Evidence routes

| Route | Implementation | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PARAMETRIC` | Deterministic model-knowledge fixture | Enabled |
| `EPISODIC_MEMORY` | Local user-specific memory with staleness metadata | Enabled |
| `BM25` | Sparse retrieval from corpus statistics | Enabled |
| `DENSE` | Deterministic signed feature hashing for semantic retrieval | Enabled |
| `STRUCTURED` | Bounded graph traversal with document provenance | Enabled |
| `FROZEN_WEB` | Versioned web-style snapshots for temporal evaluation | Enabled |
| `LIVE_WEB` | External retrieval interface | Disabled |

All routes implement the same operations:

```text
availability -> estimate -> probe -> acquire -> health -> close
```

Failures such as timeout, privacy denial, unavailable source, malformed result, and empty result
remain explicit in the trace.

## Quick start

### Docker Compose

```bash
git clone https://github.com/pxnkit/evidroute.git
cd evidroute
docker compose up --build
```

| Service | Address |
| --- | --- |
| Research console | [http://localhost:8080](http://localhost:8080) |
| OpenAPI documentation | [http://localhost:8000/docs](http://localhost:8000/docs) |
| Health endpoint | [http://localhost:8000/healthz](http://localhost:8000/healthz) |

Reference query:

```text
According to the latest snapshot, which Dresden venue will host the fictional Elbe AI Systems Workshop?
```

Expected deterministic result:

```text
Selected route: FROZEN_WEB
Answer: TU Dresden
Citation: frozen_web:elbe_workshop_t1
```

The example uses fictional MiniRoute data and does not represent a real-world factual claim.

Stop the services with:

```bash
docker compose down
```

## Development setup

Required versions:

- Python 3.12
- Node.js 22
- pnpm 11.9

### Windows PowerShell

```powershell
./scripts/setup.ps1
```

Start the API:

```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m uvicorn evidroute.api:app --reload --port 8000
```

Start the web application in a second terminal:

```powershell
Set-Location apps/web
pnpm dev
```

### POSIX or WSL

```bash
make setup
python -m uvicorn evidroute.api:app --reload --port 8000
```

Start the web application in a second terminal:

```bash
cd apps/web
pnpm dev
```

The development server is available at [http://localhost:5173](http://localhost:5173).

## API surface

| Method | Endpoint | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/healthz` | Service health |
| `GET` | `/v1/routes` | Route capabilities and availability |
| `GET` | `/v1/source-health` | Current source-health state |
| `POST` | `/v1/query` | Execute the sequential routing policy |
| `POST` | `/v1/route-preview` | Inspect candidates without acquisition |
| `POST` | `/v1/feedback` | Record decision feedback |
| `GET` | `/v1/traces/{trace_id}` | Retrieve a decision trace |
| `GET` | `/v1/traces/{trace_id}/export` | Export a canonical JSON trace |
| `POST` | `/v1/corpora` | Register a validated local corpus |
| `POST` | `/v1/snapshots/activate` | Select a frozen source snapshot |
| `POST` | `/v1/recalibrate` | Refit the selective-risk controller |
| `GET` | `/v1/models` | List model metadata |
| `GET` | `/v1/config` | Read the active public configuration |

Request and response schemas are available through the OpenAPI interface.

## Evaluation and reproducibility

MiniRoute is a synthetic benchmark included with the repository. Its cases cover direct lookup,
lexical and semantic retrieval, structured reasoning, temporal updates, stale memory,
contradictory sources, ambiguity, privacy constraints, prompt injection, source outages, and
distribution shift.

Run the complete reference experiment:

```bash
python -m evidroute.cli reproduce-mini --output artifacts/reproduce-mini
```

The command performs the following operations:

1. rebuilds deterministic retrieval indices;
2. generates forced-route potential outcomes;
3. trains the CPU potential-outcome router;
4. calibrates the selective-risk controller;
5. evaluates fixed and adaptive routing policies;
6. runs deterministic source-shift scenarios; and
7. generates Markdown, CSV, JSON, and SVG artifacts.

The committed smoke report validates system integration and artifact generation. It is not a
claim of performance on external datasets.

## Validation

GitHub Actions applies the following checks to every push and pull request:

| Backend | Frontend | Containers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ruff | ESLint | API image build |
| Strict mypy | TypeScript compiler | Web image build |
| Pytest | Vitest | Read-only runtime configuration |
| Branch coverage threshold of 75% | Production Vite build | Health checks |
| Deterministic smoke experiment | Frozen pnpm lockfile | Dropped Linux capabilities |

Current workflow status is available in
[GitHub Actions](https://github.com/pxnkit/evidroute/actions/workflows/ci.yml).

## Repository layout

| Path | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| [`apps/api`](apps/api) | FastAPI entry point |
| [`apps/web`](apps/web) | React, TypeScript, and Vite application |
| [`src/evidroute`](src/evidroute) | Core routing, evidence, risk, evaluation, security, and tracing packages |
| [`data/mini_route`](data/mini_route) | Synthetic benchmark fixtures |
| [`configs`](configs) | Experiment, router, shift, and paper configurations |
| [`scripts`](scripts) | Setup, validation, evaluation, and artifact commands |
| [`tests`](tests) | Unit, integration, failure-injection, security, and API tests |
| [`paper`](paper) | LaTeX manuscript scaffold and generated assets |
| [`reports`](reports) | Model card, data statement, ethics report, scope ledger, and smoke results |

## Research context

The design is informed by research directions presented in ACL 2025, EMNLP 2025, NeurIPS 2025,
and ICML 2026 manuscripts on uncertainty-aware retrieval, search control, information foraging,
and conversational agents over unstructured knowledge.

EvidRoute is an original implementation. It is not an official reproduction and does not reuse
source code, private data, or reported experimental results from those works. The detailed
relationship to prior work is documented in
[`docs/related-work.md`](docs/related-work.md) and [`paper/references.bib`](paper/references.bib).

## Limitations

- MiniRoute is synthetic, small, and intended for integration testing.
- The parametric route is a deterministic fixture rather than a production language model.
- Live web retrieval is disabled in the reference configuration.
- Calibration guarantees are invalidated when source shift is detected.
- Public benchmark experiments in [`configs/paper`](configs/paper) remain unrun.
- The repository is a research prototype and has not been qualified for production use.

## Data and security

The reference experiment operates entirely on redistributable synthetic data. The optional
τ-Knowledge adapter accepts a user-provided private archive path at runtime. Private documents,
tasks, policies, traces, archives, and generated checkpoints are excluded from version control,
Docker images, CI, and public artifacts.

Relevant documents:

- [`reports/data_statement.md`](reports/data_statement.md)
- [`docs/threat-model.md`](docs/threat-model.md)
- [`reports/ethics.md`](reports/ethics.md)

## Documentation

| Document | Scope |
| --- | --- |
| [`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md) | Components, data flow, and invariants |
| [`docs/routes.md`](docs/routes.md) | Route contracts and selection rules |
| [`docs/reproducibility.md`](docs/reproducibility.md) | Deterministic experiment procedure |
| [`docs/threat-model.md`](docs/threat-model.md) | Trust boundaries and mitigations |
| [`docs/related-work.md`](docs/related-work.md) | Research context and differentiation |
| [`reports/model_card.md`](reports/model_card.md) | Router behavior and limitations |
| [`reports/data_statement.md`](reports/data_statement.md) | Dataset composition and handling |
| [`reports/research_scope.md`](reports/research_scope.md) | Implemented, partial, and unrun claims |

## Contributing

Contribution requirements are defined in [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md). Substantive
changes should preserve route typing, deterministic failure behavior, trace completeness, and
the distinction between executed and proposed experiments.

## Citation

Citation metadata is provided in [`CITATION.cff`](CITATION.cff). Publications that discuss the
underlying research directions should cite the original manuscripts separately.

## License

EvidRoute is distributed under the [MIT License](LICENSE).

documents.title: evidroute — docs/architecture.md
documents.content:
# Architecture

EvidRoute models evidence acquisition as a bounded sequential decision process. At every step,
the router may acquire from one feasible source or stop with `ANSWER`, `ASK_USER`, or
`ABSTAIN`.

```text
Query + budget + risk target + snapshot
                  |
            decision features
                  |
       probes + health + policy scorer
                  |
       conservative utility ranking
                  |
     acquire one typed evidence bundle
                  |
  normalize -> deduplicate -> detect conflict
                  |
       answer + citation + risk check
             |             |
           stop       acquire next route
```

## Components

| Component | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `models.py` | Strict schemas for budgets, evidence, candidates, decisions, and traces |
| `routes/` | Stable adapter contract and seven route implementations |
| `routing/policy.py` | Decision-time scoring, feasibility, value of information, stop rule |
| `routing/learned.py` | CPU potential-outcome utility model trained from forced routes |
| `synthesis/` | Evidence-only answer selection, deduplication, conflict policy |
| `risk/` | One-sided selective-risk bounds and source-shift detection |
| `counterfactual/` | Forced-route potential outcomes, oracle, and atomic regret |
| `observability/` | Local SQLite traces, feedback, canonical JSON export |
| `api.py` | FastAPI transport, validation, upload guardrails, SSE |
| `apps/web` | React console for decisions, evidence, conflicts, budgets, and replay |

## Route contract

Each route exposes `availability`, `estimate`, `probe`, `acquire`, `health`, and `close`.
Acquisition returns a normalized `EvidenceBundle` with typed failure codes. Probes are included
in the decision trace and treated as costed observations; no hidden retrieval label is used at
decision time.

## Offline implementation

BM25 is implemented from corpus statistics. Dense retrieval uses deterministic signed feature
hashing, making the smoke path CPU-only and reproducible. Structured retrieval performs bounded
graph traversal with source-document provenance. Frozen web uses versioned snapshots. The live
web adapter is deliberately unavailable in the default configuration.

## Invariants

1. An answer in verified mode must cite normalized, safe evidence.
2. Every route call spends its estimate from a multidimensional budget.
3. Source failure, privacy denial, and malformed/no-result states are typed.
4. Trace export includes the configuration hash, source versions, model versions, and timing.
5. Shift detection invalidates the calibration guarantee instead of silently reusing it.

documents.title: evidroute — docs/adr/0001-offline-first.md
documents.content:
# ADR 0001: Credential-free offline reference path

- Status: accepted
- Date: 2026-07-23

## Decision

The default system must run without API keys or network access. External web evidence is modeled
with frozen, versioned snapshots; a live route exists only as a disabled typed adapter.

## Consequences

Smoke tests are deterministic, inexpensive, and safe to run in CI. They do not demonstrate live
web performance. A future live provider requires a new threat review, provider-specific
reliability measurements, and recalibration.

documents.title: evidroute — docs/adr/0002-risk-and-shift.md
documents.content:
# ADR 0002: Conservative selective risk with explicit shift invalidation

- Status: accepted
- Date: 2026-07-23

## Decision

Answer acceptance uses a one-sided Wilson upper bound on the unsupported-or-incorrect loss.
Calibration metadata names the loss, confidence, sample size, threshold, snapshot, and
guarantee status. Detected source or error-rate shift changes the status to
`unavailable_under_shift`.

## Consequences

The system may abstain more often than a point-estimate threshold. The bound is a transparent
prototype controller, not a universal distribution-free guarantee under arbitrary dependence.
Small or shifted strata require abstention, pooled fallback, or explicit recalibration.

documents.title: evidroute — docs/related-work.md
documents.content:
# Related work and design synthesis

EvidRoute is an original implementation inspired by research directions in the four
manuscripts below. It is not an official reproduction, and no source implementation, private
data, or reported experimental result from those works was copied into this repository.

- Moskvoretskii et al., *Adaptive Retrieval without Self-Knowledge? Bringing Uncertainty Back
  Home* (ACL 2025), motivates explicit comparison between adaptive retrieval and uncertainty
  estimation, including efficiency rather than answer quality alone.
- Wu et al., *Search Wisely* (EMNLP 2025), frames over-search and under-search through
  uncertainty. EvidRoute therefore records stop decisions, route costs, and both missed and
  unnecessary acquisition behavior.
- Qian and Liu, *Scent of Knowledge* (NeurIPS 2025), treats iterative retrieval as information
  foraging. EvidRoute's sequential policy uses a transparent information-value term and permits
  multiple evidence acquisitions.
- Shi et al., *τ-Knowledge* (ICML 2026 manuscript), evaluates conversational agents that combine
  unstructured knowledge, tools, policy, and user interaction. EvidRoute includes `ASK_USER`,
  privacy/policy failures, and a local-only archive adapter without redistributing private data.

The distinct research question here is whether a policy can choose among heterogeneous
evidence and interaction sources under an explicit risk target, source shift, and constrained
budget. The key unit of analysis is route regret against forced-route potential outcomes, not
only final exact match.

See `paper/references.bib` for the bibliography and `reports/research_scope.md` for the claim
ledger.

documents.title: evidroute — docs/reproducibility.md
documents.content:
# Reproducibility

The credential-free MiniRoute path is the executable reference experiment.

```bash
python -m evidroute.cli reproduce-mini --output artifacts/reproduce-mini --seed 17
```

The run writes forced-route outcomes, a learned router checkpoint, calibration data, raw
predictions, aggregate metrics, corruption manifests, drift results, CSV/SVG report assets, and
`run_manifest.json`.

The manifest records:

- Python, platform, and relevant package versions;
- random seed and validated engine configuration;
- configuration SHA-256;
- hashes of every bundled MiniRoute input;
- Git commit and worktree status, when available;
- snapshot, index, and schema versions.

Determinism applies to the bundled CPU routes and MiniRoute input. Wall-clock timings, operating
system scheduling, dependency solver output, and floating-point behavior across different
architectures may vary. A public benchmark run is a separate experiment and must retain its
license, download provenance, original split, preprocessing hash, and evaluation command.

## Scientific claim boundary

The generated smoke report demonstrates that the pipeline executes and emits auditable
artifacts. It is not evidence that EvidRoute outperforms published systems. The repository does
not report a public benchmark result until the corresponding run exists.

documents.title: pxnkit — README.md
documents.content:
Hi, I'm Pankit Brahmkhatri 👋

MSc Computer Science at TU Dresden

## About me I design and evaluate adaptive agent systems that decide when to retrieve evidence, what to retain in memory, how to update from feedback, and when to act or abstain. My work sits at the intersection of information retrieval, agent memory, test-time learning, and search-guided reasoning. I focus on systems whose decisions remain grounded in evidence, resilient to stale or conflicting memory, and measurable through reproducible experiments. ## Research focus | Area | Problems I care about | |---|---| | **Adaptive evidence seeking** | Query planning, source routing, hybrid retrieval, cross-encoder reranking, provenance, evidence sufficiency, and budget-aware stopping | | **Agent memory and test-time learning** | Episodic, semantic, and procedural memory; consolidation; temporal validity; forgetting; experience replay; feedback; and online adaptation | | **Search-guided reasoning** | Best-of-N, beam and tree search, verifier-guided trajectories, process feedback, uncertainty estimation, adaptive compute, and calibrated act or abstain decisions | | **Reliable agent execution** | Structured tool schemas, durable checkpoints, idempotent actions, pre-action verification, sandboxing, prompt injection testing, and memory poisoning resistance | ## Technical profile ### Core toolkit

I treat retrieval, memory, reasoning, and execution as one connected system. Each layer needs clear interfaces, traceable decisions, and evaluation that reflects real failure modes. | Layer | Technologies and methods | |---|---| | **Engineering and data contracts** | Python, Git, Linux, PostgreSQL, `uv`, Ruff, mypy, Pydantic, FastAPI, pytest, Docker, and GitHub Actions | | **Models and adaptation** | PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, Datasets, Accelerate, Sentence Transformers, PEFT and LoRA, TRL, vLLM, replay buffers, adapter versioning, and retention or forgetting evaluation | | **Retrieval and evidence routing** | BM25 and Lucene, dense embeddings, reciprocal-rank fusion, cross-encoder reranking, FAISS, PostgreSQL and pgvector, OpenSearch, filtered ANN and HNSW, query decomposition, source routing, provenance, and evidence-sufficiency stopping | | **Agent memory and data plane** | Episodic, semantic, and procedural memory; append-only and bi-temporal event stores; PostgreSQL for durable state; Redis for caching; DuckDB with Parquet and Arrow for trajectory data; graph storage when traversal is a core requirement | | **Agent runtime and reasoning search** | LangGraph or explicit state machines, structured tool schemas, Model Context Protocol, durable checkpoints, timeouts, retries, idempotency, best-of-N, beam and tree search, MCTS, verifier models, uncertainty scoring, and adaptive compute allocation | | **Evaluation and observability** | `ir_datasets` and BEIR-style corpora, `ir_measures`, pytrec_eval, ranx, Recall@k, MRR, nDCG, MLflow, OpenTelemetry traces, Brier and ECE calibration, risk-coverage curves, latency, and cost budgets | | **Security and reliable action** | Sandboxed tools, least privilege, ACL-aware retrieval, secrets management, append-only provenance, policy gates, prompt injection tests, memory poisoning tests, and deterministic replay | ## Current research directions - Learning retrieval and memory policies instead of relying only on fixed RAG pipelines - Routing information between working context, external memory, and model updates - Adapting from interaction feedback and failed trajectories while measuring retention and forgetting - Using retrieval-grounded verification for long-horizon reasoning - Maintaining memory freshness, provenance, temporal validity, and contradiction handling - Building poisoning-resistant memory and prompt-injection-aware retrieval - Calibrating when an agent should search, continue reasoning, act, ask for help, or abstain ## Collaboration I am interested in collaborating on agent memory benchmarks, learned retrieval policies, test-time adaptation, search-guided reasoning, agent evaluation, and reliable tool-using systems. I am especially interested in work that combines a clear research question with reproducible systems, measurable failure modes, and honest evaluation.

documents.title: trace-mem — README.md
documents.content:
# TRACE-Mem

TRACE-Mem is an executable reliability layer for persistent AI agents. It
maps how faults travel from memory writes to irreversible tool actions, finds
the stages that caused a failed run, and verifies risky actions before they
are committed.

The included claims workflow is a complete reference implementation. A case
evolves across sessions: an address changes, coverage is updated, and the
preferred contact channel changes. TRACE-Mem records those facts in a
bi-temporal memory, injects controlled faults at five stages, replays failures
with targeted repairs, learns an interaction-aware risk model, and applies a
verification gate before the final action.

## What is implemented

- Append-only, bi-temporal memory with `active`, `superseded`, and `disputed`
  states.
- Fault injection at memory write, consolidation, retrieval, reasoning, and
  tool-action stages.
- Trace-level signals for write gaps, active-memory conflicts, stale
  retrievals, inconsistent reasoning, and mutated tool payloads.
- Counterfactual replay that repairs one stage at a time and records whether
  the failed action recovers.
- A causal reliability map that measures pairwise fault interaction lift.
- An interaction-aware risk model learned from historical traces.
- A pre-commit risk gate that verifies source events and rebuilds the proposed
  action when risk exceeds a configurable threshold.
- An offline HTML operations dashboard plus JSON and CSV exports.

## Run

TRACE-Mem uses only the Python standard library. Python 3.10 or newer is
required; no API keys or external services are needed.

```powershell
python .\trace_mem.py --output-dir .\results
Start-Process .\results\dashboard.html
```

Useful options:

```powershell
python .\trace_mem.py --seed 7 --train-runs 5000 --test-runs 1500 --risk-threshold 0.55
```

Generated artifacts:

- `dashboard.html`: reliability, intervention, and trace explorer
- `results.json`: complete machine-readable run output
- `scenario_results.csv`: per-case operating metrics
- `reliability_map.csv`: pairwise causal interaction map

## Test

```powershell
python -m unittest discover -s .\tests -v
```

## Runtime flow

1. The agent stages a tool action instead of immediately committing it.
2. TRACE-Mem derives reliability signals from the complete memory-to-action
   trace.
3. The learned model estimates failure risk, including interactions between
   signals.
4. Low-risk actions commit normally. High-risk actions are verified against
   the source-event adapter, rebuilt, and then committed.
5. Failed historical traces can be replayed with targeted repairs to produce
   causal attributions and improve verification policy.

The built-in claims cases contain generated data and serve as a reproducible
local workload. The runtime classes are domain-independent: another agent can
provide its own source events, staged action payload, evaluator, and verifier
without changing the reliability model.
